audio.text: Franz Kafka wurde 1883 in Prag geboren und arbeitete fast sein ganzes Berufsleben lang bei einer Versicherung. Geschrieben hat er vor allem nachts. Kurz vor seinem Tod bat er seinen Freund Max Brod, alle Manuskripte zu verbrennen. Brod hat sich zum Glück nicht daran gehalten: Er gab die Romane heraus, und so wurde Kafka erst nach seinem Tod weltberühmt.

choices: He burned them, as Kafka had asked.
He sold them to an insurance company.
He gave them back to Kafka's family in Prague.
questions.explanation: "Brod hat sich zum Glück nicht daran gehalten: Er gab die Romane heraus" – he didn't keep to Kafka's wish and published (herausgeben) the novels. The insurance is where Kafka worked; burning was what Kafka had asked for.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio book tip. What did Kafka not want, according to the speaker?

audio.text: Unser Buchtipp der Woche ist ein Klassiker: Die Verwandlung von Franz Kafka. Ein Handlungsreisender wacht eines Morgens als riesiges Ungeziefer auf. Was für ein Tier er genau ist, erfahren wir nie. Kafka wollte nicht einmal, dass das Insekt auf dem Umschlag des Buches abgebildet wird. Die Leserinnen und Leser sollten es sich selbst vorstellen.

choices: A picture of the insect on the book cover
A translation of the story into other languages
That the hero should be a travelling salesman
That readers should imagine the animal themselves
questions.explanation: "Kafka wollte nicht einmal, dass das Insekt auf dem Umschlag des Buches abgebildet wird": he didn't want the insect shown on the cover. He did want readers to imagine it themselves ("sollten es sich selbst vorstellen"), so the last choice is the opposite of what was said.

questions.stem: Build the sentence (indirect question in the narration).
questions.prompt: He wondered what the boss would say.
questions.explanation: The indirect question starts with "was", and the verb cluster goes to the end with the finite verb last: "sagen würde". From the past point of view of the story, the future "wird" becomes "würde".

questions.stem: Which sentence is erlebte Rede rather than indirect speech?
choices: Sie sagte, sie müsse es ihm am nächsten Tag sagen.
Sie dachte, dass sie es ihm am nächsten Tag sagen müsse.
Sie fragte sich, ob sie es ihm am nächsten Tag sagen solle.
Morgen musste sie es ihm sagen, ganz bestimmt!
questions.explanation: In erlebte Rede the time word stays as the character thinks it ("morgen") even with a past verb, and there's no introducing verb; the exclamation "ganz bestimmt!" is the character's voice. The other three have an introducing verb (sagte, dachte, fragte sich) and shift "morgen" to "am nächsten Tag", as indirect speech does.

questions.stem: A friend says: "Für den Antrag brauche ich ein Formular, das ich nur mit dem Antrag bekomme." Which comment fits?
questions.explanation: "kafkaesk" describes exactly this: an absurd, circular situation, typically bureaucratic, that is hard to escape. "vorbildlich" (exemplary), "übersichtlich" (clear, easy to follow) and "bequem" (convenient) say the opposite of what the friend is experiencing.

questions.stem: In an old text you read: "Es ward Nacht." What does "ward" correspond to in modern German?
questions.explanation: "ward" is an old Präteritum of werden (singular), today "wurde": "Es wurde Nacht" (Night fell). It isn't a misprint for "war", and it's not the present "wird" or the Konjunktiv II "würde".

questions.stem: Miller says: "Ich hätt meine Tochter mehr koram nehmen sollen." What does he mean?
choices: I would like to take my daughter to task more.
I had to take my daughter to task more.
I will take my daughter to task more.
I should have taken my daughter to task more.
questions.explanation: "hätt" is "hätte" with the e dropped; "hätte ... nehmen sollen" is the Konjunktiv II past of a modal verb with the double infinitive: regret about the past, "should have". "koram nehmen" (from Latin coram) means to take someone to task.

questions.stem: Match the terms with their meanings.
choices: one of the large parts of a play
text that describes the setting and the actions
a speech by one character alone on stage
the set, the design of the stage
the person who wrote the play
questions.explanation: der Akt = act; die Regieanweisung = stage direction; der Monolog = monologue; das Bühnenbild = the set. The person who wrote the play is der Dramatiker or die Dramatikerin.

questions.stem: Which feature is typical of an open drama like Woyzeck?
choices: Short, loosely connected scenes and jumps in time and place
Exactly five acts with a strict cause-and-effect chain
Elevated verse spoken only by nobles
A happy ending with a wedding
questions.explanation: The open drama breaks the classical rules: short scenes that can almost stand alone, jumps in time and place, everyday or dialect language. Five strict acts belong to the closed drama; a happy ending with a wedding is typical of comedy.

questions.stem: What was new about the bourgeois tragedy (das bürgerliche Trauerspiel)?
choices: It was the first kind of play written in prose rather than verse.
Middle-class people could be the tragic heroes.
It was performed only at court.
questions.explanation: The old Ständeklausel reserved tragedy for kings and nobles. The bourgeois tragedy of the 18th century (Lessing, Schiller's Kabale und Liebe) made middle-class people and their families the centre of a tragedy. Prose existed before it, and it certainly doesn't end happily.

questions.stem: Miller fears: "Der Präsident bekommt Wind." What does he mean?
choices: The President is catching a cold.
The President will find out about it.
The President is going on a journey.
questions.explanation: "Wind bekommen (von etwas)" means to get wind of something, to find out about it, just like the English idiom. It's still used today: "Die Presse hat Wind von der Sache bekommen."

questions.stem: Complete the set phrase with the old dative -e: "Ich gehe jetzt nach ___." (Haus)
questions.explanation: The dative -e of older German survives in set phrases: nach Hause, zu Hause, im Grunde. "nach Haus" is also heard in speech, but "nach Hause" is the standard written form.

questions.stem: Listen to the theatre review on the radio. What is on the stage in this production?

audio.text: Die neue Inszenierung von Kabale und Liebe am Stadttheater verzichtet fast ganz auf ein Bühnenbild. Auf der leeren, schwarzen Bühne stehen nur ein Tisch und ein Cello. Die Hauptrolle der Luise spielt eine junge Schauspielerin, die erst seit diesem Jahr zum Ensemble gehört. Am Ende gab es langen Applaus.

choices: A table and a cello, nothing else
A large photo of the President
questions.explanation: "Auf der leeren, schwarzen Bühne stehen nur ein Tisch und ein Cello": the production does almost without a set ("verzichtet fast ganz auf ein Bühnenbild"). The other objects aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen to two people after a performance of Woyzeck. What does the second speaker think?

audio.text: Also für mich ist Woyzeck einfach ein Mörder. Er bringt eine Frau um, Punkt. – Das ist mir zu einfach. Er wird doch von allen ausgenutzt: vom Hauptmann, vom Doktor mit seinen Experimenten. Am Ende ist er selbst ein Opfer. Das macht seine Tat nicht besser, aber man versteht sie.

choices: Woyzeck is simply a murderer, and that's the end of it.
The doctor is the real murderer.
The play is too simple to be interesting.
Woyzeck is also a victim, which makes his act understandable but not better.
questions.explanation: The second speaker says "Das ist mir zu einfach" (that's too simple for me), calls Woyzeck "selbst ein Opfer" (a victim himself) and adds "Das macht seine Tat nicht besser, aber man versteht sie". The first choice is the first speaker's view.

questions.stem: Build Miller's regret in modern German.
questions.prompt: I should have brought up my daughter more strictly.
questions.explanation: "hätte" stands in position 2, and the double infinitive goes to the end with the modal last: "erziehen sollen". "sollen" (should) expresses the regret; "hätte ... erziehen können" would mean "could have".

questions.stem: Which pairing of play, author and period is correct?
choices: Kabale und Liebe – Schiller – Sturm und Drang
questions.explanation: Schiller wrote Kabale und Liebe (1784) as a young writer of the Sturm und Drang. Woyzeck (1836–37) is by Georg Büchner and belongs to the Vormärz. Lessing wrote the first well-known bourgeois tragedies, but not Woyzeck.

questions.stem: Woyzeck says: "Unsereins ist doch einmal unselig in der und der andern Welt." What does "unsereins" mean?
questions.explanation: "unsereins" (colloquial, still used today) means "people like us, the likes of us". Woyzeck says that poor people are wretched in this world and the next.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Im zweiten Akt hat Lady Milford ihren ersten Auftritt.
In der dritte Szene streiten Vater und Sohn.
Die Akte über den Fall liegt beim Gericht.
Der Bösewicht des Stücks heißt Wurm.
questions.explanation: After "in der" (dative, feminine) the adjective needs the weak ending -en: "in der dritten Szene". The third sentence is correct because "die Akte" (file) is a different, feminine noun from "der Akt" (act). Lady Milford does first appear in act 2, and Wurm is the villain.

questions.stem: What is the Bundesrat in Switzerland?
choices: The chamber in which the cantons are represented
The federal government, made up of seven members
The chamber elected by the people
questions.explanation: In Switzerland the Bundesrat is the government: seven members who decide together. The cantons are represented in the Ständerat, and the people elect the Nationalrat. In Germany and Austria, by contrast, the Bundesrat is the chamber of the Länder.

questions.stem: Which EU institution formally proposes new laws?
questions.explanation: Only the Commission can formally propose an EU law ("Ein Gesetzesvorschlag wird von der Kommission vorgelegt"). Parliament and the Council of the EU then decide on it; the European Council sets the general direction but doesn't pass laws.

questions.stem: What is the difference between an EU Verordnung and an EU Richtlinie?
choices: A Verordnung applies directly; a Richtlinie must first be implemented in national law.
A Richtlinie applies directly; a Verordnung must first be implemented in national law.
A Verordnung is only a recommendation; a Richtlinie is binding.
A Verordnung is made by the Länder, a Richtlinie by the EU.
questions.explanation: A regulation (Verordnung) applies in all member states at once, like a national law. A directive (Richtlinie) sets a goal that each member state must implement (umsetzen) in its own law by a deadline. Both are binding EU law.

questions.stem: Complete with the past participle: "Österreich ist 1995 der EU ___." (beitreten)
questions.explanation: "beitreten" is separable (bei-) and strong, with sein in the perfect: "ist beigetreten". It takes the dative: "der EU beitreten".

questions.stem: Complete with the missing preposition: "Großbritannien ist 2020 ___ der EU ausgetreten."
questions.explanation: "austreten aus + dative": aus der EU, aus der Partei, aus dem Verein. The noun works the same way: der Austritt aus der EU.

questions.stem: Which of these is not an institution of the European Union?
questions.explanation: The Europarat (Council of Europe) in Strasbourg is a separate, older organization with 46 member states, known for the European Convention on Human Rights. The Council of the EU (ministers) and the European Council (heads of government) are both EU institutions, despite the similar names.

questions.stem: Match each institution with its description.
choices: the parliament elected by the people in Germany
the chamber elected by the people in Austria
the chamber that represents the cantons
the seven-member federal government of Switzerland
questions.explanation: The Bundestag and the Austrian Nationalrat are the chambers elected by the people; the Swiss Ständerat represents the cantons (two seats each, one for each of the six former half-cantons); a Landesregierung governs one Land. The seven-member Swiss government is the Bundesrat.

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. What happens after the new rules have been adopted?

audio.text: Brüssel. Die Europäische Kommission hat heute einen Vorschlag für neue Regeln zum Schutz von Verbrauchern beim Onlinekauf vorgelegt. Bevor die Regeln gelten können, müssen das Europäische Parlament und der Rat zustimmen. Da es sich um eine Richtlinie handelt, haben die Mitgliedstaaten nach der Verabschiedung zwei Jahre Zeit, sie in nationales Recht umzusetzen.

choices: They apply immediately in all member states.
The Commission votes on them a second time.
The member states have two years to implement them in national law.
Each member state decides whether to adopt them at all.
questions.explanation: "Da es sich um eine Richtlinie handelt, haben die Mitgliedstaaten nach der Verabschiedung zwei Jahre Zeit, sie in nationales Recht umzusetzen." A directive must be implemented by a deadline; only a regulation applies immediately, and implementing it isn't optional.

questions.stem: Listen to the voice message from a colleague in Zurich. Why are many companies based in the canton of Zug?

audio.text: Hallo Jana, kurz zu deiner Frage von heute Morgen: In der Schweiz legen die Kantone ihre Steuersätze selbst fest. Zug verlangt besonders niedrige Steuern, deshalb haben dort so viele Firmen ihren Sitz. Der Bund kann den Kantonen da nichts vorschreiben. Wenn du noch Fragen hast, ruf mich einfach an!

choices: Because the federal government sends them there
Because Zug has particularly low taxes, which the canton sets itself
Because the EU pays for their offices
Because Zug is the Swiss capital
questions.explanation: "Die Kantone legen ihre Steuersätze selbst fest. Zug verlangt besonders niedrige Steuern, deshalb haben dort so viele Firmen ihren Sitz." The federal level can't prescribe tax rates to the cantons ("Der Bund kann den Kantonen da nichts vorschreiben"). Switzerland isn't in the EU, and the seat of the federal government is Bern.

questions.stem: Build the sentence (modal passive in a subordinate clause).
questions.prompt: The deadline is important because the directive has to be implemented in national law.
questions.explanation: In the weil clause the whole verb cluster goes to the end in the order participle – werden – modal: "umgesetzt werden muss". The modal "muss" is the finite verb and comes last.

questions.stem: Choose the right relative pronoun: "Der Ständerat ist die Kammer, ___ die Kantone vertreten sind."
questions.explanation: "in" for where something is takes the dative, and "die Kammer" is feminine, so the relative pronoun is "der": "die Kammer, in der ...". "in die" is accusative (direction), "in dem" would be masculine or neuter, and "die" alone leaves out the preposition.

questions.stem: Which nominal phrase means the same as "Nachdem die Richtlinie verabschiedet worden ist, ..."?
questions.explanation: "nachdem" (after) becomes the preposition "nach" + dative, and the passive clause becomes a noun with a genitive: "nach der Verabschiedung der Richtlinie". "vor" means before, "wegen" because of and "trotz" despite.

questions.stem: What does "die Freizügigkeit" mean in EU politics?
choices: The right of EU citizens to live and work in any member state
Free public transport in the EU
The free choice of a political party
questions.explanation: "die Freizügigkeit" is the free movement of people: EU citizens may live and work in any member state. It is one of the four freedoms of the single market (goods, services, capital, people).

questions.stem: An Austrian newspaper writes "im Jänner". What is "Jänner"?
choices: A dialect word that shouldn't appear in a newspaper
An old word that is no longer used
The standard Austrian word for January
questions.explanation: "der Jänner" is an Austriacism: standard German in Austria, used in newspapers, schools and offices. German is pluricentric, so Austrian standard words are as correct as the words of Germany.

questions.stem: Match the Austrian words with the words used in Germany.
questions.explanation: Paradeiser = Tomate, Marille = Aprikose, Erdapfel = Kartoffel, Topfen = Quark. The Austrian word for Sahne is (Schlag)obers.

questions.stem: Match the Swiss words with the words used in Germany.
questions.explanation: Velo = Fahrrad, parkieren = parken, Trottoir = Bürgersteig (Gehweg), Billett = Fahrkarte. Many Helvetisms come from French. The Swiss word for the Abitur is die Matura.

questions.stem: How is "die Straße" spelled in Switzerland? Type the noun with its article.
questions.explanation: Switzerland and Liechtenstein don't use ß at all and always write ss: die Strasse, gross, der Fuss. The official spelling rules allow this explicitly for Switzerland.

questions.stem: A colleague from Graz says: "Ich bin zwei Stunden im Wartezimmer gesessen." What is true?
choices: It's a typical learner's mistake; it must be "habe gesessen".
It's only used in dialect, never in standard German.
It's standard in Austria, Switzerland and southern Germany.
It's an old form from the 18th century.
questions.explanation: In the south of the German-speaking area, sitzen, stehen and liegen form the perfect with sein: "ich bin gesessen". In northern and central Germany "ich habe gesessen" is the norm. Both are standard in their regions.

questions.stem: What does diglossia mean in German-speaking Switzerland?
choices: Swiss German dialects are spoken in almost every situation; standard German is used mainly for writing and formal speech.
German and French are spoken equally in every canton.
Only older people still speak dialect.
Standard German is spoken at home, dialect only in writing.
questions.explanation: In German-speaking Switzerland there are two clearly separate forms with their own domains: Swiss German for speaking (at home, at work, on local radio) and standard German mainly for writing, school lessons and the news. The last choice reverses the roles.

questions.stem: Which word is a Teutonism, a word typical of Germany but not of Austria or Switzerland?
questions.explanation: "die Sahne" is the word of Germany; Austria says (Schlag)obers and Switzerland Rahm. "das Velo" is Swiss, "der Topfen" Austrian and "die Matura" Austrian and Swiss.

questions.stem: Listen to the conversation at a market in Vienna. What does the customer buy?

audio.text: Grüß Gott! Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Marillen und ein Viertelkilo Topfen. Ich mache morgen Marillenknödel. – Sehr gern. Und Paradeiser vielleicht? Die sind heuer besonders gut. – Nein, danke, heute nicht.

questions.explanation: "ein Kilo Marillen und ein Viertelkilo Topfen": Marillen are apricots and Topfen is quark. She is offered Paradeiser (tomatoes) but says "Nein, danke, heute nicht".

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement in Zurich. What will not be allowed from Monday?

audio.text: Wegen Bauarbeiten ist das Trottoir an der Bahnhofstrasse ab Montag gesperrt. In dieser Zeit dürfen keine Velos vor dem Bahnhof parkiert werden. Bitte benutzen Sie den Veloparkplatz an der Seefeldstrasse. Wir danken für Ihr Verständnis.

choices: Taking the train from the station
Parking bikes in front of the station
Crossing the street at the station
questions.explanation: "In dieser Zeit dürfen keine Velos vor dem Bahnhof parkiert werden": no bikes (Velos) may be parked in front of the station. Cyclists should use the bike park at the Seefeldstrasse instead. The pavement (Trottoir) on the Bahnhofstrasse is closed.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Austrian standard German.
questions.prompt: We sat in the inn all evening.
questions.explanation: In Austria sitzen takes sein in the perfect: "Wir sind ... gesessen". The participle goes to the end. The time phrase usually comes before the place phrase, but "im Gasthaus den ganzen Abend" is also possible, and either phrase can start the sentence (Den ganzen Abend sind wir im Gasthaus gesessen).

questions.stem: In an Austrian office a colleague says: "Nimm dir doch einen Sessel!" What is she offering?
questions.explanation: In Austria "der Sessel" is an ordinary chair (in Germany: der Stuhl). In Germany "der Sessel" is an armchair, which makes it a false friend between the varieties.

questions.stem: Which statement about "das Schweizerdeutsch" is correct?
choices: It is the name of the standard German written in Swiss newspapers.
It is a group of dialects, such as Zurich and Bern German, used for speaking.
It is spoken only in the French-speaking part of Switzerland.
Learners are expected to speak it in Swiss shops.
questions.explanation: "Schweizerdeutsch" means the Swiss German dialects, which differ from region to region. Newspapers are written in Swiss standard German (Schweizer Hochdeutsch), and learners are expected to speak standard German.

questions.stem: Complete with the Konjunktiv I of "kommen": "Der Korrespondent sagt, er ___ morgen aus Kairo zurück."
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I is the infinitive stem + -e for er/sie/es: komm- + -e = komme. "kommt" is the indicative, which in a news report would sound as if the writer vouched for it. "käme" is the Konjunktiv II, used only when the Konjunktiv I looks like the indicative (not the case for er). "kam" is the simple past.

questions.stem: Complete with the Konjunktiv I of "fahren": "Die Ministerin erklärt, sie ___ am Montag nach Brüssel."
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I never changes the stem vowel: fahr- + -e = fahre. The a → ä change belongs only to the du and er forms of the indicative (du fährst, sie fährt), so "fähre" doesn't exist. "führe" is the Konjunktiv II of fahren (and also a form of führen).

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Redakteure sagen, sie ___ mit dem Text zufrieden."
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I of sein for sie (plural) is "seien". "sind" is the indicative. "sein" is the infinitive, a very common spelling mistake, and "seie" doesn't exist: the singular is "sei" with no -e.

questions.stem: Type the Konjunktiv I of "es gibt": "Die Polizei sagt, es ___ keine Hinweise auf einen Anschlag."
questions.explanation: es gibt becomes es gebe: the infinitive stem geb- + -e, with no e → i change. "es gebe" is one of the most frequent forms in news German.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct formal indirect speech?
choices: Sie sagte, dass sie sei krank.
questions.explanation: Without dass, the reported clause has the verb in position 2: "sie sei krank". Inside quotation marks, the speaker's exact words stay in the indicative ("Ich bin krank"). After dass, the verb must go to the end (dass sie krank sei). "seie" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Anna sagt: „Ich arbeite in der Redaktion.“ Which is the correct report in formal German?
choices: Anna sagt, ich arbeite in der Redaktion.
Anna sagt, sie arbeite in der Redaktion.
Anna sagt, sie arbeitete in der Redaktion.
Anna sagt, dass sie arbeite in der Redaktion.
questions.explanation: The pronoun shifts to the reporter's point of view (ich → sie) and the verb goes into the Konjunktiv I (arbeite). "ich arbeite" would mean that you, the reporter, work there. "arbeitete" looks like the simple past, and the dass clause needs the verb at the end.

questions.stem: On Tuesday you report what a spokesman said on Monday: „Wir veröffentlichen die Zahlen morgen.“ Complete: "Der Sprecher sagte am Montag, die Firma veröffentliche die Zahlen ___."
questions.explanation: His "morgen" was Tuesday, the day after he spoke, so in a later report it becomes "am nächsten Tag". Keeping "morgen" would now mean Wednesday. "am Tag zuvor" and "gestern" point backwards to Sunday and Monday.

questions.stem: Why does a news report write "Der Bürgermeister sagt, die Stadt habe kein Geld" rather than "…, die Stadt hat kein Geld"?
choices: Because habe is the past tense of haben.
Because the Konjunktiv I is more polite.
Because the sentence describes something unreal.
Because the Konjunktiv I marks the claim as the mayor's, and the writer stays neutral.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I signals reported speech: the newspaper passes on the claim without vouching for it. It's not a past tense (the time is the same as the statement) and it doesn't express unreality or politeness; those are jobs of the Konjunktiv II.

questions.stem: Listen to the traffic news. What did the police spokesman say?

audio.text: Ein Sprecher der Polizei sagte am Morgen, die Bundesstraße zwölf sei nach einem Unfall in beide Richtungen gesperrt. Die Sperrung dauere voraussichtlich bis zum Mittag. Es gebe eine Umleitung über Neustadt.

choices: The road is closed until about midday, and there is a diversion via Neustadt.
The road will be closed from midday, and Neustadt is also closed.
Only one direction is closed, and drivers should wait.
The road is open again, but there are delays near Neustadt.
questions.explanation: The spokesman said the road "sei … in beide Richtungen gesperrt" (closed in both directions), the closure "dauere voraussichtlich bis zum Mittag" (will probably last until midday) and "es gebe eine Umleitung über Neustadt" (there is a diversion via Neustadt). The Konjunktiv I forms sei, dauere and gebe show it is all his report.

questions.stem: Listen and type the verb you hear: "Die Firma sagt, sie ___ keine Pläne für einen Umzug."

audio.text: Die Firma sagt, sie habe keine Pläne für einen Umzug.

questions.explanation: You hear "habe", the Konjunktiv I of haben for er/sie/es. The indicative would be "hat", the Konjunktiv II "hätte". In a news report, "habe" passes on the company's statement neutrally.

questions.stem: Which Konjunktiv I form is clearly different from the indicative?
questions.explanation: "er wisse" can't be anything but Konjunktiv I (indicative: er weiß). The others look exactly like the indicative: ich komme, wir haben, sie können. That's why in practice the Konjunktiv I is used mainly in the er/sie/es form and for sein; lesson 2 shows what replaces the others.

questions.stem: A spokesman spoke last week. Match his words to what a report written today would say.
questions.explanation: When a report is written later or somewhere else, time and place words shift to the reporter's point of view: heute → an diesem Tag (or am selben Tag), gestern → am Tag zuvor (am Vortag), morgen → am nächsten Tag (am folgenden Tag), hier → dort.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in formal German (reported speech, no dass).
questions.prompt: The spokeswoman says the press office is closed today.
questions.explanation: Without dass, the reported clause has main-clause order: the Konjunktiv I "sei" in position 2 and the participle "geschlossen" at the end. "heute" can also start the reported clause (heute sei die Pressestelle geschlossen). "seie" and "sein" are not forms of the Konjunktiv I.

questions.stem: Build the sentence with dass, in formal German.
questions.prompt: The editor says that the article is too long.
questions.explanation: After dass, the verb goes to the end of the clause: "dass der Artikel zu lang sei". The Konjunktiv I of sein for er/sie/es is "sei", without -e.

questions.stem: What is a "Leitartikel"?
choices: The first news report on the front page.
An article in which the paper gives its opinion on an important issue.
A report bought from a news agency.
questions.explanation: der Leitartikel is the editorial: the leading opinion piece of a newspaper. The front page is die Titelseite, an agency report comes from a Nachrichtenagentur, and a reader's letter is ein Leserbrief.

questions.stem: The editor-in-chief says: „Die Quellenlage ist noch zu dünn.“ What does she mean?
choices: There isn't enough reliable evidence yet to publish the story.
The article is too short for the front page.
The paper doesn't have enough subscribers.
The informant is too young to be quoted.
questions.explanation: die Quellenlage is the state of the available sources. "Zu dünn" (too thin) means there isn't enough reliable information yet, for example only one anonymous source. It says nothing about length, subscribers (Abonnements) or the informant's age.

questions.stem: Read the report: "Die Lokalzeitung „Hollerbacher Bote“ erscheint ab Januar nur noch dreimal pro Woche. Der Verlag begründete die Entscheidung mit den hohen Kosten für Papier und Vertrieb. Die Auflage sei in den letzten zehn Jahren um ein Drittel gesunken. Gleichzeitig wachse die Zahl der digitalen Abonnements. Die Redaktion werde nicht verkleinert, versicherte der Chefredakteur. Man wolle die Berichterstattung im Internet sogar ausbauen." Which information does the writer present as a fact, not as someone's statement?
choices: The circulation has fallen by a third.
From January the paper will appear only three times a week.
The editorial team will not be reduced.
questions.explanation: The first sentence is in the indicative (erscheint): the writer states it as a fact. (The reporting verbs begründete and versicherte are indicative too, but they only say who said something.) The circulation figure (sei … gesunken), the growth in subscriptions (wachse) and the promise about the team (werde nicht verkleinert) are in the Konjunktiv I: they are the publisher's and the editor's claims.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Er sagt, er gebe nicht auf.
Sie sagt, sie fähre morgen nach Rom.
Er sagt, er lese jeden Tag Zeitung.
Sie sagt, es gebe noch Hoffnung.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I keeps the infinitive vowel: fahren → sie fahre, not "fähre". gebe (geben), lese (lesen) and es gebe are all correct: no vowel change, ending -e.

questions.stem: Listen to the conversation in a newsroom. What does the second speaker doubt?

audio.text: Was hat die Pressestelle gesagt? – Die Sprecherin sagt, der Bürgermeister sei krank und komme heute nicht ins Rathaus. Aber ich habe ihn heute Morgen beim Bäcker gesehen.

choices: That the press office has a spokeswoman.
That the mayor is really ill.
questions.explanation: He reports the press office's claim in the Konjunktiv I (der Bürgermeister sei krank, komme nicht), then adds a fact in the indicative: he saw the mayor at the baker's this morning. So he doubts that the mayor is ill. The spokeswoman herself isn't said to be ill.

questions.stem: Type the Konjunktiv I of "können": "Die Stadt sagt, man ___ die Zahlen noch nicht nennen."
questions.explanation: Modal verbs keep their infinitive vowel in the Konjunktiv I: könn- + -e = könne. The indicative is "kann", the Konjunktiv II "könnte". man takes the er/sie/es form.

questions.stem: Complete in formal German: "Die Zeugen sagen, sie ___ nichts gesehen."
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I for sie (plural) would be "haben", which looks exactly like the indicative. The replacement rule takes the Konjunktiv II instead: "hätten". "habe" is singular, and "hatten" is the simple past (it would make the sentence a past perfect).

questions.stem: The tenants say: „Wir zahlen die Miete pünktlich.“ Which report follows the replacement rule?
choices: Die Mieter erklären, sie zahlen die Miete pünktlich.
Die Mieter erklären, sie zahlten die Miete pünktlich.
Die Mieter erklären, sie würden die Miete pünktlich zahlen.
Die Mieter erklären, sie zahle die Miete pünktlich.
questions.explanation: "sie zahlen" is both Konjunktiv I and indicative, so it can't show reported speech. The Konjunktiv II "zahlten" of a weak verb looks like the simple past, so it can't either. The last resort is würde + infinitive: "sie würden … zahlen". "zahle" is singular.

questions.stem: The witness said: „Ich sah den Angeklagten am Bahnhof.“ Which report is correct?
choices: Der Zeuge sagte, er habe den Angeklagten am Bahnhof gesehen.
Der Zeuge sagte, er sei den Angeklagten am Bahnhof gesehen.
Der Zeuge sagte, er sah den Angeklagten am Bahnhof.
Der Zeuge sagte, er sehe den Angeklagten am Bahnhof.
questions.explanation: Indirect speech has one past form: Konjunktiv I of haben/sein + Partizip II, whatever tense the speaker used. sehen takes haben: "er habe … gesehen". "sei … gesehen" uses the wrong helping verb, "sah" is just the indicative past, and "sehe" moves the event into the present.

questions.stem: The defendant said: „Ich bin um zehn nach Hause gegangen.“ Complete: "Die Angeklagte sagte, sie ___ um zehn nach Hause gegangen."
questions.explanation: gehen forms its perfect with sein, so the past in indirect speech is "sei … gegangen". "habe" and "hätte" use the wrong helping verb, and "ist" is the indicative.

questions.stem: The lawyers said: „Wir werden in Berufung gehen.“ Type the missing verb: "Die Anwälte kündigten an, sie ___ in Berufung gehen."
questions.explanation: The future in indirect speech uses the Konjunktiv I of werden. For sie (plural), "werden" looks like the indicative, so it's replaced by the Konjunktiv II "würden". In the singular it would be "er werde in Berufung gehen".

questions.stem: The judge asked the witness: „Kennen Sie den Angeklagten?“ Which report is correct?
choices: Die Richterin fragte die Zeugin, ob kenne sie den Angeklagten.
Die Richterin fragte die Zeugin, ob sie den Angeklagten kenne.
Die Richterin fragte die Zeugin, dass sie den Angeklagten kenne.
Die Richterin fragte die Zeugin, kenne sie den Angeklagten?
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with ob, and the verb goes to the end: "ob sie den Angeklagten kenne". dass introduces statements, not questions, and an indirect question has no question mark and no inverted order.

questions.stem: The prosecutor asked: „Wo waren Sie am Abend des 3. Mai?“ Complete: "Der Staatsanwalt fragte, ___."
choices: wo war er am Abend des 3. Mai
ob er am Abend des 3. Mai gewesen sei
wo er am Abend des 3. Mai gewesen sei
wo er am Abend des 3. Mai sei gewesen
questions.explanation: A question-word question keeps its question word (wo) and puts the verb at the end, in the past form of indirect speech: "gewesen sei". "ob" would turn it into a yes/no question, "wo war er" has main-clause order, and "sei gewesen" reverses the two verbs.

questions.stem: The judge said politely: „Bitte setzen Sie sich.“ Which formal report keeps the meaning?
choices: Die Richterin bat ihn: setzen Sie sich, bitte.
Die Richterin bat ihn, er wolle sich setzen.
Die Richterin bat ihn, dass er setze sich.
Die Richterin bat ihn, er möge sich setzen.
questions.explanation: A polite request is reported with the Konjunktiv I of mögen: "er möge sich setzen". (An infinitive with zu, "sich zu setzen", would also work.) "er wolle" means he wanted to, which changes the meaning; an imperative can't stand in indirect speech; and after dass the verb must go to the end.

questions.stem: Which sentence fits a court report in a newspaper?
choices: Er hat gesagt, dass er unschuldig ist.
Der Angeklagte sagte, er sei unschuldig.
Er sagt, er ist unschuldig, ne?
questions.explanation: A written report uses the Konjunktiv I (er sei), which shows that this is the defendant's claim. The indicative after dass and the spoken Konjunktiv II "wär" are normal in conversation, and "ne?" is a spoken tag question.

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail from a colleague. What happened in court?

audio.text: Hallo Lea, hier ist Ben. Ich bin gerade aus dem Gericht raus. Die Richterin hat den Angeklagten freigesprochen. Sie hat gesagt, die Beweise würden nicht reichen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft will aber in Berufung gehen. Ruf mich an, wenn du den Text brauchst.

choices: The defendant was acquitted, but the prosecution wants to appeal.
The defendant was convicted, and the defence wants to appeal.
The trial was postponed because evidence was missing.
The defendant was acquitted, and the verdict is final.
questions.explanation: "freigesprochen" means acquitted. Ben reports the judge's reason in everyday spoken style (die Beweise würden nicht reichen: the evidence wasn't enough). "Die Staatsanwaltschaft will aber in Berufung gehen": the prosecution wants to appeal, so the verdict isn't final.

questions.stem: Listen and complete: "Der Zeuge sagte aus, er ___ den Mann nie ___."

audio.text: Der Zeuge sagte aus, er habe den Mann nie gesehen.

questions.explanation: "er habe … gesehen" is the past in indirect speech: Konjunktiv I of haben + Partizip II. aussagen means to testify.

questions.stem: Listen to two people discussing a verdict. Why does the second speaker think it is fair?

audio.text: Ich finde das Urteil viel zu mild. Zwei Jahre auf Bewährung für so einen Betrug! – Moment mal. Er war vorher nie verurteilt worden, und er hat den ganzen Schaden zurückgezahlt. Ich finde das gerecht.

choices: Because the defendant was found innocent.
Because the prisons are too full.
Because he had no previous convictions and has paid back all the damage.
Because the judge gave him a heavy fine instead.
questions.explanation: The second speaker says "Er war vorher nie verurteilt worden" (he had never been convicted before) and "er hat den ganzen Schaden zurückgezahlt" (he has paid back all the damage). The sentence was two years "auf Bewährung" (suspended), not a fine, and he was not found innocent.

questions.stem: Match each person in a criminal trial to what they do.
questions.explanation: The Staatsanwältin (public prosecutor) brings the Anklage; the Verteidiger (defence lawyer) defends the Angeklagte, the person on trial; the Richterin (judge) gives the Urteil; the Zeuge (witness) sagt aus.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in formal German.
questions.prompt: The witnesses said they had seen nothing.
questions.explanation: Past in indirect speech: helping verb + Partizip II. For sie (plural), the Konjunktiv I "haben" looks like the indicative, so the replacement rule gives "hätten". "habe" is singular.

questions.stem: Build the indirect question in formal German.
questions.prompt: The judge asked whether he had understood the verdict.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with ob, and the verbs go to the end: Partizip II, then the helping verb "habe". verstehen takes haben, so "sei" is wrong; dass introduces statements, not questions.

questions.stem: A newspaper writes: "Der Angeklagte wurde freigesprochen." What happened to him?
questions.explanation: freisprechen means to acquit: the court found him not guilty (der Freispruch). Convicted is verurteilt, charged is angeklagt.

questions.stem: Read the report: "Im Rechtsstreit zwischen einer Mieterin und ihrem Vermieter hat das Amtsgericht am Donnerstag ein Urteil gefällt. Die Mieterin hatte geklagt, weil ihre Wohnung seit Monaten feucht sei. Der Vermieter sei für den Schimmel verantwortlich, erklärte ihr Anwalt. Der Vermieter dagegen behauptete, die Mieterin lüfte zu selten. Das Gericht gab der Klage teilweise recht: Die Miete wird um 15 Prozent gesenkt." What did the landlord claim?
choices: That the flat was not damp at all.
That the tenant didn't air the flat often enough.
That the rent was too low.
That the tenant's lawyer was responsible for the mould.
questions.explanation: "Der Vermieter dagegen behauptete, die Mieterin lüfte zu selten": the tenant airs the flat too rarely. The Konjunktiv I lüfte marks this as his claim. The last sentence, in the indicative, is the court's decision, which the paper reports as a fact.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Sie sagte, sie habe den Brief bekommen.
Er sagte, er sei sofort gekommen.
Er sagte, er habe nach Hause gegangen.
questions.explanation: gehen takes sein in the perfect, so the past in indirect speech is "er sei nach Hause gegangen". The other sentences are correct: bekommen takes haben, kommen takes sein, and "seien" is always visible, so it never needs replacing.

questions.stem: The defendants said: „Wir wissen nichts.“ Type the missing verb: "Die Angeklagten erklärten, sie ___ nichts."
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I "sie wissen" looks like the indicative, so the Konjunktiv II replaces it: "wüssten" (with umlaut). "wussten" without umlaut is the simple past.

questions.stem: A friend tells you on the phone: „Tom hat gesagt, er wär krank.“ What does she mean?
choices: Tom said he was ill; she's just passing it on.
Tom would be ill if he went to work.
Tom was ill earlier but is fine now.
questions.explanation: In everyday speech the Konjunktiv II (wär, short for wäre) is a normal way to report what someone said. It doesn't mean "unreal" here: she simply passes on Tom's statement, as a written report would with "er sei krank".

questions.stem: What does "Der Sänger soll sehr reich sein." mean?
choices: The singer must be very rich.
The singer wants to be very rich.
The singer is said to be very rich.
The singer is supposed to become very rich.
questions.explanation: Subjective sollen passes on hearsay: people say he's very rich. "must be" would be muss (the speaker's own conclusion), "wants to be" is objective wollen, and "is supposed to become" would need werden.

questions.stem: What does "Sie will nichts gesehen haben." mean?
choices: She wants to have seen nothing.
She claims not to have seen anything.
She is said to have seen nothing.
questions.explanation: With a perfect infinitive, wollen is subjective: the subject claims something about herself, and the speaker doubts it. "Is said to" would be soll, "must have" would be muss. A literal "wants to have seen" makes no sense in German either.

questions.stem: Which sentence expresses the highest degree of certainty?
questions.explanation: muss expresses a confident conclusion (he must be ill). dürfte means "probably", kann and könnte only "possibly". From most to least sure: muss > dürfte > kann/könnte.

questions.stem: In which sentence is the modal verb used subjectively?
choices: Du musst um acht da sein.
Sie muss den Schlüssel verloren haben.
questions.explanation: "Sie muss den Schlüssel verloren haben" is the speaker's conclusion about the past (she must have lost the key): a subjective use, with a perfect infinitive. The others describe obligation, a wish and an instruction for the subject: objective uses.

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "Die Ministerin soll schon zurückgetreten ___."
questions.explanation: zurücktreten forms its perfect with sein (sie ist zurückgetreten), so the perfect infinitive is "zurückgetreten sein". "haben" would be the wrong helping verb.

questions.stem: What does "Das muss nicht stimmen." mean?
choices: That is supposed to be true.
questions.explanation: muss nicht means "not necessarily", not "must not". "Must not" in the sense of a prohibition is darf nicht; "can't be true" is kann nicht stimmen.

questions.stem: Complete with the modal that means "probably": "Die Affäre ___ ihm schaden."
questions.explanation: dürfte, the Konjunktiv II of dürfen, is a typical newspaper way to say "probably". The indicative darf has no such meaning (it means "is allowed to"). will would mean the affair wants to harm him, and subjective mag would express a possibility or concession ("may harm him"), not probability.

questions.stem: Rewrite with a modal verb: "Angeblich hat der Präsident Geld genommen."
choices: Der Präsident soll Geld genommen haben.
Der Präsident will Geld genommen haben.
Der Präsident hat Geld nehmen sollen.
Der Präsident sollte Geld genommen haben.
questions.explanation: angeblich (allegedly) = subjective sollen in the present + perfect infinitive: "soll … genommen haben". "will" would mean he himself claims it; "hat … nehmen sollen" means he was supposed to take money (objective); "sollte" doesn't express hearsay about the past.

questions.stem: Listen to the neighbours talking. What does the new neighbour herself say?

audio.text: Hast du schon gehört? Die neue Nachbarin soll früher im Fernsehen gewesen sein. Sie selbst will aber nie vor der Kamera gestanden haben. Ich glaube, das muss ein Missverständnis sein.

choices: That she used to be on TV.
That she works in television now.
That she has never been in front of a camera.
That it must be a misunderstanding.
questions.explanation: "Sie selbst will aber nie vor der Kamera gestanden haben": subjective wollen reports her own claim that she has never stood in front of a camera. "Soll … gewesen sein" is what other people say; "muss ein Missverständnis sein" is the speaker's own conclusion.

questions.stem: Listen and type the sentence you hear.

audio.text: Er soll gelogen haben.

questions.explanation: "Er soll gelogen haben" = he is said to have lied: subjective sollen + perfect infinitive (gelogen haben, from lügen).

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. Which information does the report present as certain?

audio.text: Nach Informationen unserer Redaktion soll der Konzern jahrelang Abgaswerte gefälscht haben. Ein Sprecher des Unternehmens wies die Vorwürfe am Abend zurück. Experten halten einen großen Imageschaden für wahrscheinlich.

choices: The company falsified emissions data for years.
The company's image has already been badly damaged.
questions.explanation: "Ein Sprecher … wies die Vorwürfe zurück" is in the indicative: the reporter states it as a fact. The falsification is only reported (soll … gefälscht haben), and the image damage is only "wahrscheinlich" (probable) according to experts.

questions.stem: Match each subjective modal to a word with a similar meaning.
questions.explanation: soll = angeblich (it's said), muss = bestimmt (I'm sure), dürfte = vermutlich (probably), könnte = vielleicht (possibly). keinesfalls (by no means) would match kann nicht.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: He is said to have resigned.
questions.explanation: Subjective sollen in position 2, the perfect infinitive at the end: Partizip II + sein (zurücktreten takes sein). "haben" is the wrong helping verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: She can't have written the letter.
questions.explanation: "kann nicht" + perfect infinitive expresses that something in the past is impossible. The modal is in position 2, nicht comes before the infinitive group, and the perfect infinitive (geschrieben haben) goes to the end.

questions.stem: Complete the police report: "Die Polizei hat den ___ Täter festgenommen; die Ermittlungen laufen noch."
questions.explanation: mutmaßlich means "suspected, presumed": he's probably the culprit, but no court has decided yet. That's the standard word in police reports. vermeintlich would suggest the belief is mistaken (he probably isn't the culprit), and the other adjectives don't express the uncertainty.

questions.stem: What does "vertuschen" mean in "Die Firma hat versucht, den Unfall zu vertuschen."?
questions.explanation: vertuschen means to cover up or hush up. To reveal is enthüllen, to deny officially is dementieren (noun: das Dementi), and to forge is fälschen (die Fälschung).

questions.stem: Read the gossip item: "Seit Wochen wird über die Ehe der Schauspielerin Lena Ostrowski spekuliert. Sie soll sich von ihrem Mann getrennt haben, berichten mehrere Zeitschriften. Ostrowski selbst sagte am Freitag in einer Talkshow, sie wolle über ihr Privatleben nicht sprechen. Ihr Mann will die Gerüchte schon vor einem Monat dementiert haben, ein solches Dementi ist allerdings nirgends zu finden. Fest steht nur: Das Paar wurde seit März nicht mehr zusammen gesehen." Which statement does the writer present as a fact?
choices: The actress has separated from her husband.
Her husband denied the rumours a month ago.
The actress talked about her private life on Friday.
The couple hasn't been seen together since March.
questions.explanation: "Fest steht nur" (the only certain thing is) introduces the fact: they haven't been seen together since March. The separation is hearsay (soll … getrennt haben), the denial is the husband's doubtful claim (will … dementiert haben), and the actress said she would not talk about her private life.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
questions.explanation: zurücktreten takes sein in the perfect, so the perfect infinitive is "zurückgetreten sein": "Sie soll zurückgetreten sein." lügen and wissen take haben, and "Das kann nicht stimmen" (that can't be true) is correct.

questions.stem: Type the Konjunktiv II of "dürfen" that means "probably": "Der neue Chefredakteur ___ über sechzig sein."
questions.explanation: dürfte (er/sie/es form, with umlaut) expresses probability: he's probably over sixty. "durfte" without umlaut is the simple past (was allowed to).

questions.stem: Which subordinate clause is correct?
choices: Ich habe gelesen, dass er soll gelogen haben.
Ich habe gelesen, dass er gelogen soll haben.
Ich habe gelesen, dass soll er gelogen haben.
Ich habe gelesen, dass er gelogen haben soll.
questions.explanation: In a subordinate clause the conjugated modal goes to the very end, after the perfect infinitive: "gelogen haben soll". Such clauses are correct but heavy; in a main clause it's simply "Er soll gelogen haben."

questions.stem: Complete: "Bis 2040 ___ wir das Darlehen getilgt haben."
questions.explanation: The Futur II is werden + Partizip II + haben/sein: "werden … getilgt haben" (will have repaid). "würden" would make it a Konjunktiv II (would have), and haben/sind can't combine with "getilgt haben" at the end.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wenn du ankommst, wird der Zug schon abgefahren ___."
questions.explanation: abfahren forms its perfect with sein (der Zug ist abgefahren), so the Futur II is "wird … abgefahren sein". "worden" belongs to the passive.

questions.stem: Kim is late. Her colleague says: „Sie wird den Bus verpasst haben.“ What does he mean?
choices: She has to catch the bus.
She would have missed the bus.
She has probably missed the bus.
questions.explanation: Without a future time phrase, the Futur II usually expresses an assumption about the past: "she'll have missed the bus" = she has probably missed it. "would have" would be Konjunktiv II (hätte … verpasst).

questions.stem: Herr Kaya isn't answering the phone. Complete: "Er ___ schon nach Hause gegangen sein."
questions.explanation: "Er wird schon nach Hause gegangen sein" is a Futur II assumption: he has probably gone home already. "ist … gegangen sein" and "hat … gegangen sein" are not possible combinations; "würde … gegangen sein" isn't a normal assumption.

questions.stem: Type the participle of "einzahlen": "In zwanzig Jahren werden Sie insgesamt 72.000 Euro ___ haben."
questions.explanation: einzahlen is separable, so ge- goes between the prefix and the stem: eingezahlt. Futur II: werden … eingezahlt haben (will have paid in).

questions.stem: Which subordinate clause is correct?
choices: Ich hoffe, dass wir das Haus bis 2040 abbezahlt werden haben.
Ich hoffe, dass wir das Haus bis 2040 werden abbezahlt haben.
Ich hoffe, dass wir das Haus bis 2040 haben abbezahlt werden.
Ich hoffe, dass wir das Haus bis 2040 abbezahlt haben werden.
questions.explanation: In a subordinate clause the conjugated werden goes to the very end, after the perfect infinitive: Partizip II + haben + werden ("abbezahlt haben werden").

questions.stem: What is the most natural way to say "Bis Freitag werde ich den Bericht geschrieben haben." in conversation?
choices: Bis Freitag schrieb ich den Bericht.
Bis Freitag hatte ich den Bericht geschrieben.
Bis Freitag habe ich den Bericht geschrieben.
Bis Freitag würde ich den Bericht schreiben.
questions.explanation: In speech, the perfect with a future time phrase (bis Freitag) replaces the Futur II: "Bis Freitag habe ich den Bericht geschrieben." The simple past and past perfect refer to the past, and "würde … schreiben" means "would write".

questions.stem: Which sentence is an assumption about the past?
choices: Bis Juni wird sie die Prüfung bestanden haben.
Sie wird die Prüfung wohl schon gestern bestanden haben.
Sie wird im Juni Prüfungen haben.
questions.explanation: "gestern" and "wohl" show a guess about something already past: she probably passed the exam yesterday. "Bis Juni …" is a completed future (use 1), and the other two are Futur I about the future.

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. What does Frau Lenz assume?

audio.text: Hallo Herr Kaya, hier ist Frau Lenz von der Bank. Ich habe Ihnen letzte Woche die Unterlagen zur Altersvorsorge geschickt. Sie werden sie inzwischen bekommen haben. Bis Ende des Monats werden wir alles vorbereitet haben, dann können wir den Vertrag unterschreiben. Rufen Sie mich bitte zurück.

choices: That Herr Kaya has received the documents by now.
That Herr Kaya has already signed the contract.
That the documents got lost in the post.
That Herr Kaya will call before the end of the month.
questions.explanation: "Sie werden sie inzwischen bekommen haben" is a Futur II assumption about the past: you'll have received them by now. "Bis Ende des Monats werden wir alles vorbereitet haben" is a completed future: the contract can be signed after that.

questions.stem: Listen and type the sentence you hear.

audio.text: Bis dahin werde ich alles abbezahlt haben.

accept: Bis dahin werde ich alles abbezahlt haben
questions.explanation: "Bis dahin werde ich alles abbezahlt haben" = by then I will have paid everything off. Futur II: werde + abbezahlt (separable ab-, no ge- because of be-) + haben.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio report. According to the report, what will have happened to savers in ten years?

audio.text: Die Inflation dürfte im nächsten Jahr bei rund zwei Prozent liegen. Wer sein Geld jetzt auf dem Sparkonto lässt, wird in zehn Jahren deutlich an Kaufkraft verloren haben.

choices: They will have earned high interest.
They will have paid ten per cent inflation.
Their banks will have closed their savings accounts.
They will have lost a lot of purchasing power.
questions.explanation: "wird in zehn Jahren deutlich an Kaufkraft verloren haben": they will have lost significant purchasing power (die Kaufkraft). The two per cent is the expected inflation for next year, introduced with dürfte (probably).

questions.stem: Match the financial terms.
questions.explanation: die Aktie = share, die Anleihe = bond, der Fonds = fund, das Darlehen = loan, die Rendite = return on an investment. An instalment is die Rate.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: She will probably have forgotten the appointment.
questions.explanation: Futur II as an assumption: wird in position 2, vergessen haben at the end (vergessen takes haben). wohl can stand before or after the object, and the object can also start the sentence (Den Termin wird sie wohl vergessen haben).

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: I'm sure that he will have paid off the loan by then.
questions.explanation: In the dass clause the verb cluster goes to the end in the order Partizip II + haben + wird. The time phrase "bis dahin" can come before or after the object.

questions.stem: What is "eine Rücklage"?
choices: Money set aside for emergencies or future costs.
questions.explanation: die Rücklage is a reserve: money put aside, for example for repairs or emergencies. A loan is das Darlehen, a company pension die Betriebsrente, an instalment die Rate.

questions.stem: What does "tilgen" mean in "Wir tilgen das Darlehen in monatlichen Raten."?
questions.explanation: ein Darlehen tilgen means to repay a loan, here in monthly instalments (Raten). To take out a loan is ein Darlehen aufnehmen; to invest is anlegen.

questions.stem: Read the advice column: "Frage einer Leserin: Ich bin 30 und verdiene gut, aber ich habe noch nichts für meine Altersvorsorge getan. Ist es zu spät? – Antwort: Nein, im Gegenteil. Wenn Sie jetzt monatlich 200 Euro in einen breit gestreuten Fonds anlegen, werden Sie bis zur Rente 37 Jahre lang eingezahlt haben. Wichtig ist aber zuerst eine Rücklage von drei Monatsgehältern für Notfälle. Und fragen Sie Ihren Arbeitgeber, ob er eine Betriebsrente anbietet; oft zahlt er einen Teil dazu." What should the reader do first?
choices: Build up a reserve of three months' salary.
Ask her employer about a company pension.
Invest 200 euros a month in a fund.
Take out a loan for a flat.
questions.explanation: "Wichtig ist aber zuerst eine Rücklage von drei Monatsgehältern": first, an emergency reserve of three months' salary. The fund and the company pension are further steps; nothing is said about a loan.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Bis Mai werden wir umgezogen sein.
Er wird den Brief bekommen haben.
questions.explanation: gehen takes sein, so the Futur II is "Sie wird schon gegangen sein." umziehen also takes sein (umgezogen sein), while bekommen and schaffen take haben.

questions.stem: Type the missing verb: "Wir rechnen damit, dass die Zinsen bis dahin gestiegen sein ___."
questions.explanation: Futur II in a subordinate clause: Partizip II + sein + the conjugated werden at the end. die Zinsen is plural, so "werden".

questions.stem: The adviser said: „Ich werde bis Juni alles erledigt haben.“ Which formal report is correct?
choices: Sie sagte, sie werde bis Juni alles erledigt haben.
Sie sagte, sie wird bis Juni alles erledigt haben.
Sie sagte, sie habe bis Juni alles erledigt werden.
Sie sagte, sie würde bis Juni alles erledigt.
questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the Futur II takes the Konjunktiv I of werden: "sie werde … erledigt haben". "wird" is the indicative, and the other two are not possible verb combinations.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Zufolge dem Bericht sinken die Quoten.
Dem Bericht laut sinken die Quoten.
Dem Bericht zufolge sinken die Quoten.
Des Berichts zufolge sinken die Quoten.
questions.explanation: zufolge is a postposition: it follows its noun, which is in the dative: "dem Bericht zufolge" (not the genitive "des Berichts", and not "zufolge dem Bericht"). laut goes before the noun (laut dem Bericht).

questions.stem: A report says: "Die Ministerin räumte ein, dass Fehler gemacht wurden." What does "einräumen" tell you?
choices: She stressed it as especially important.
questions.explanation: einräumen means to concede or admit something you'd rather not say. To stress is betonen, to deny is bestreiten, to announce in advance is ankündigen.

questions.stem: Complete with the verb that means "denied": "Der Minister ___, das Geld genommen zu haben."
questions.explanation: bestreiten (bestritt) means to deny, and it takes a zu-infinitive with a perfect infinitive here: "bestritt, das Geld genommen zu haben". betonen means to stress, versichern to assure, ankündigen to announce.

questions.stem: Complete: "Um Mitternacht ___ die Jury den Sieger."
questions.explanation: verkünden is used for making a decision or result public: "Die Jury verkündete den Sieger." ankündigen means to announce something in advance, and it is separable, so in a main clause it would be "kündigte … an". bekräftigen (reaffirm) and bestreiten (deny) don't fit.

questions.stem: Complete with the simple past of "ankündigen": "Der Sender ___ eine neue Talkshow ___."
questions.explanation: ankündigen is separable and weak: in a main clause the stem goes to position 2 (kündigte) and the prefix an goes to the end: "Der Sender kündigte eine neue Talkshow an."

questions.stem: Which sentence is the most neutral for a news report?
choices: Die Intendantin behauptete, der Sender müsse sparen.
Die Intendantin erklärte, der Sender müsse sparen.
Die Intendantin versuchte zu beschwichtigen: Der Sender müsse angeblich sparen.
Die Intendantin gab endlich zu, der Sender müsse sparen.
questions.explanation: erklären simply passes the statement on. behaupten (claim), beschwichtigen (play down), angeblich (allegedly) and "gab endlich zu" (finally admitted) all add the writer's judgement, which belongs in an opinion piece.

questions.stem: Which form is the standard choice in written German? "Wie ein Sprecher des Senders mitteilte, ___ die Sendung abgesetzt."
questions.explanation: The wie-clause already names the source, so the main clause is normally in the indicative: "ist die Sendung abgesetzt". A Konjunktiv I (sei, werde) is sometimes seen there but is redundant; wäre would suggest something unreal.

questions.stem: In which phrase is "gemäß" used correctly?
questions.explanation: gemäß means "in accordance with" a rule, regulation or agreement: gemäß der Hausordnung (in accordance with the house rules). For a person's statement, use laut or nach Angaben: laut der Ministerin, nach Angaben des Augenzeugen.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio news. What did the lorry driver say?

audio.text: Wie die Polizei am Abend mitteilte, ist die Autobahn zwischen Hollerbach und Neustadt wieder frei. Nach Angaben eines Sprechers wurde bei dem Unfall niemand schwer verletzt. Der Fahrer des Lastwagens bestritt, zu schnell gefahren zu sein.

choices: That he had not been driving too fast.
That he had been driving too fast.
That nobody had been seriously hurt.
That the motorway was clear again.
questions.explanation: "Der Fahrer … bestritt, zu schnell gefahren zu sein": he denied having driven too fast. That nobody was badly hurt and that the motorway is clear come from the police, introduced with "nach Angaben eines Sprechers" and "wie die Polizei mitteilte".

questions.stem: Listen and type the missing word: "Dem Bericht ___ sinken die Einschaltquoten."

audio.text: Dem Bericht zufolge sinken die Einschaltquoten.

questions.explanation: "dem Bericht zufolge" = according to the report. zufolge follows its noun, which is in the dative.

questions.stem: Listen to two people discussing the licence fee. What does the first speaker concede at the end?

audio.text: Ich sehe kaum noch fern. Warum soll ich dann den Rundfunkbeitrag zahlen? – Weil du trotzdem Radio hörst, die Mediathek nutzt und unabhängige Nachrichten bekommst. Das kostet eben Geld. – Das mag sein. Aber dann sollte man wenigstens weniger Talkshows zeigen.

choices: That he watches a lot of TV.
That talk shows are worth the money.
That he never listens to the radio.
That the other speaker's point may be right.
questions.explanation: "Das mag sein" (that may be so) concedes the other speaker's point before "aber" introduces a new demand: fewer talk shows. He says he hardly watches TV, and he doesn't contradict that he listens to the radio.

questions.stem: Match the reporting verbs to their meanings.
questions.explanation: betonen = to stress, einräumen = to concede, bestreiten = to deny, versichern = to assure, bekräftigen = to reaffirm. "to announce in advance" would be ankündigen.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: According to the report, the ratings are falling.
questions.explanation: "Dem Bericht zufolge" (zufolge after its dative noun) can fill position 1, with the verb following in position 2, or come after the verb: Die Einschaltquoten sinken dem Bericht zufolge. With zufolge naming the source, the indicative "sinken" is normal; "sinke" would also be singular.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in formal German.
questions.prompt: The presenter stressed that the show had not been cancelled.
questions.explanation: The past passive in indirect speech is "sei … abgesetzt worden": Konjunktiv I of sein, Partizip II, and worden (not geworden) at the end.

questions.stem: What does "die Einschaltquote" measure?
choices: How long a programme is on air.
How much the licence fee costs.
How many people watch a programme.
How far a radio signal reaches.
questions.explanation: die Einschaltquote is the ratings: how many people watch (literally, switch on). Airtime is die Sendezeit, the licence fee der Rundfunkbeitrag, and reach die Reichweite.

questions.stem: Where do you find a programme "in der Mediathek"?
choices: In a shop that sells DVDs.
In the press office of a broadcaster.
In a broadcaster's online library, to stream after broadcast.
questions.explanation: die Mediathek is a broadcaster's online library, where programmes can be streamed after they have been broadcast (ausgestrahlt). A public library is eine Bibliothek or Bücherei.

questions.stem: Read the report: "Podcasts statt Radio? Einer neuen Studie zufolge hört inzwischen jeder dritte Erwachsene regelmäßig Podcasts. Laut der Studie sind die Zuhörer im Durchschnitt deutlich jünger als beim klassischen Hörfunk. Die Programmdirektorin eines großen Radiosenders betonte, das Radio habe trotzdem die größte Reichweite aller Medien. Sie räumte allerdings ein, dass der Sender bei jungen Leuten Hörer verliert. Deshalb wolle man im nächsten Jahr zehn neue Podcasts starten." What did the programme director admit?
choices: That radio has the biggest reach of all media.
That the station is losing young listeners.
That the station started ten podcasts this year.
questions.explanation: "Sie räumte allerdings ein, dass der Sender bei jungen Leuten Hörer verliert": she conceded that the station is losing young listeners. What she stressed (betonte) was radio's reach; the age of podcast listeners comes from the study; the ten podcasts are planned for next year.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Dem Bericht zufolge steigen die Preise.
questions.explanation: warnen vor takes the dative: "vor dem Medienkonsum". "den Medienkonsum" is accusative. In "vor den Gefahren" den is the dative plural, so that sentence is correct.

questions.stem: Type the preposition: "Experten warnen ___ zu viel Bildschirmzeit bei Kindern."
questions.explanation: warnen vor + dative = to warn against or of something: Experten warnen vor zu viel Bildschirmzeit.

questions.stem: How do you say "He denied having lied."?
choices: Er bestritt, nicht gelogen zu haben.
Er bestritt, dass er nicht gelogen habe.
questions.explanation: bestreiten already contains the "no": "Er bestritt, gelogen zu haben." Adding nicht reverses the meaning (he denied that he had not lied). The zu-infinitive needs zu: "gelogen zu haben".

questions.stem: An old recipe begins: "Man nehme 200 Gramm Mehl." What does it mean?
choices: People say you take 200 grams of flour.
One would take 200 grams of flour.
questions.explanation: man + Konjunktiv I is the old-style recipe instruction: "take …". It's not reported speech (there is no speaker), not a past form and not a conditional (that would be "man würde … nehmen").

questions.stem: Complete the old-style recipe: "Das Eiweiß ___ man steif."
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I keeps the infinitive vowel: schlag- + -e = schlage. "schlägt" is the indicative, "schlüge" the Konjunktiv II and "schlug" the simple past.

questions.stem: How does a German maths textbook say "Let x be any number."?
choices: Lass x eine beliebige Zahl sein.
Es ist x eine beliebige Zahl sein.
Sei x eine beliebige Zahl ist.
Es sei x eine beliebige Zahl.
questions.explanation: German maths uses the Konjunktiv I of sein for "let … be": "Es sei x eine beliebige Zahl" (or "Sei x …"). lassen isn't used this way, and the other two mix two verbs.

questions.stem: Type the missing word: "___ A und B zwei verschiedene Punkte. Dann gibt es genau eine Gerade durch A und B."
questions.explanation: There are two points, so the plural Konjunktiv I of sein is needed: "Seien A und B …". The conclusion (Dann gibt es …) is in the indicative.

questions.stem: In a discussion someone says: „Wie dem auch sei, wir müssen heute entscheiden.“ What does "Wie dem auch sei" mean?
questions.explanation: "Wie dem auch sei" (be that as it may) closes a side issue and returns to the main point. It's a fixed phrase with the Konjunktiv I sei.

questions.stem: When would you say "Gott sei Dank!"?
choices: To greet someone in the morning.
To express relief: something bad didn't happen.
questions.explanation: "Gott sei Dank" (thank God, thank goodness) expresses relief and is completely everyday, not felt as religious: "Gott sei Dank ist niemandem etwas passiert."

questions.stem: Match the phrases with the Konjunktiv I to their meanings.
questions.explanation: All four use the Konjunktiv I to express a wish or a request: Es lebe … (long live), sei es … sei es … (whether … or …), Koste es, was es wolle (whatever it costs), Man beachte … (please note). "Be that as it may" is Wie dem auch sei.

questions.stem: Listen to the old-style recipe. What should be done with the egg whites?

audio.text: Man nehme drei Eier, trenne sie und schlage das Eiweiß mit einer Prise Salz steif. Dann hebe man es vorsichtig unter den Teig.

choices: Mix them with the yolks and bake them separately.
Beat them stiff with a pinch of salt and fold them into the dough.
Add them to the dough with a teaspoon of salt and stir hard.
Separate them and keep them for another recipe.
questions.explanation: "schlage das Eiweiß mit einer Prise Salz steif" (beat the egg whites stiff with a pinch of salt), then "hebe man es vorsichtig unter den Teig" (carefully fold it into the dough). unterheben means to fold in, not to stir.

questions.stem: Listen to the maths problem. What is the answer?

audio.text: Gegeben sei ein Dreieck mit einem rechten Winkel. Die beiden kürzeren Seiten seien drei und vier Zentimeter lang. Wie lang ist die längste Seite?

questions.explanation: In a right-angled triangle a² + b² = c²: 9 + 16 = 25, so c = 5 cm. The problem uses the maths Konjunktiv I: "Gegeben sei …", "Die beiden kürzeren Seiten seien …". 25 is c², not c.

questions.stem: Build the instruction in old recipe style.
questions.prompt: Take a teaspoon of salt.
questions.explanation: The recipe formula is man + Konjunktiv I: "Man nehme …", with no vowel change. A teaspoon is der Teelöffel; der Esslöffel is a tablespoon.

questions.stem: In "Der Koch sagt, man nehme am besten frische Äpfel.", what is the Konjunktiv I "nehme"?
choices: Reported speech: it passes on what the cook says.
A recipe instruction to the reader.
questions.explanation: There's a speaker and a reporting verb (Der Koch sagt), so this is indirect speech: the cook says it's best to take fresh apples. Without "Der Koch sagt", "Man nehme frische Äpfel" would be an instruction.

questions.stem: What does "eine beliebige Zahl" mean?
questions.explanation: beliebig means "any … you like, arbitrary": "Wählen Sie eine beliebige Zahl" = choose any number. A popular number would be eine beliebte Zahl: don't confuse beliebig with beliebt.

questions.stem: A live ticker says: "72.: Novak tritt an … und trifft!" Why is it in the present tense?
choices: Because the penalty will be taken later.
Because tickers use the present for events that have just happened, to make them vivid.
Because "trifft" is a Konjunktiv I form.
Because the reporter is quoting the player.
questions.explanation: The ticker uses the historic present: past events told in the present to make them feel immediate. "trifft" is the normal indicative present of treffen (Konjunktiv I would be "treffe").

questions.stem: What has been left out of the headline "Bayern weiter souverän"?
questions.explanation: The full sentence would be "Bayern ist weiterhin souverän". Headlines often drop sein and articles (ellipsis). The subject (Bayern) is there, and souverän has no ending because it's a predicate adjective.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Von den Fans gefeiert, die Mannschaft verließ den Platz.
Von den Fans gefeiert, war das Wetter herrlich.
Gefeiert von den Fans, die Mannschaft den Platz verließ.
Von den Fans gefeiert, verließ die Mannschaft den Platz.
questions.explanation: The participle phrase fills position 1, so the verb (verließ) follows directly, then the subject. The subject must be what the participle describes: the team was celebrated, not the weather.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: „Wir sind glücklich“, hat gesagt die Trainerin.
„Wir sind glücklich“, sagte sie die Trainerin.
questions.explanation: The quote fills position 1, so the reporting verb comes next and the subject follows it: „…“, sagte die Trainerin. "hat gesagt die Trainerin" breaks the perfect word order, and "sie die Trainerin" repeats the subject.

questions.stem: The coach said: „Wir haben verdient gewonnen.“ Type the verb for the match report: "Die Trainerin sagte, ihre Mannschaft ___ verdient gewonnen."
questions.explanation: die Mannschaft is singular, so the Konjunktiv I "habe" is visible and is used: "ihre Mannschaft habe verdient gewonnen". The pronoun wir changes to ihre Mannschaft from the reporter's point of view.

questions.stem: Match the football words.
questions.explanation: der Elfmeter = penalty, das Eigentor = own goal, der Ausgleich = equalizer, der Abstieg = relegation, der Aufstieg = promotion. The referee is der Schiedsrichter or die Schiedsrichterin.

questions.stem: Listen to the ticker. Who scored?

audio.text: Siebenundsechzigste Minute: Ecke für Eichenried. Berger köpft – an die Latte! Im Gegenzug Konter Hollerbach, Novak allein vor dem Tor … und sie trifft! Zwei zu eins!

choices: Berger, with a header for Eichenried.
Nobody: the ball hit the bar.
Novak, on a counter-attack for Hollerbach.
An Eichenried player, with an own goal.
questions.explanation: Berger's header hit the bar (an die Latte). On the counter-attack (im Gegenzug, Konter), Novak was alone in front of goal "und sie trifft": she scored, making it 2–1. Typical ticker style: present tense and verbless fragments.

questions.stem: Listen to the coach after the match. How does he see the penalty?

audio.text: Natürlich bin ich enttäuscht. Wir haben in der ersten Hälfte gut gespielt, aber nach dem Ausgleich haben wir die Ordnung verloren. Den Elfmeter kann man geben. Das muss man akzeptieren.

choices: He thinks it was clearly wrong.
He thinks it was a possible decision that has to be accepted.
He says it decided the first half.
He says the referee apologized for it.
questions.explanation: "Den Elfmeter kann man geben. Das muss man akzeptieren": the penalty was a defensible decision, and you have to accept it. He blames the defeat on losing their structure after the equalizer (nach dem Ausgleich).

questions.stem: What is "die Hinrunde"?
choices: The first half of a match.
The first round of a cup competition.
The training period before the season.
The first half of the league season.
questions.explanation: die Hinrunde is the first half of the season, in which every team plays every other once; die Rückrunde is the second half. The first half of a match is die erste Halbzeit.

questions.stem: Which one is typical headline style?
choices: Die Mannschaft ist leider im Elfmeterschießen ausgeschieden, was sehr schade ist.
Es war so, dass die Mannschaft im Elfmeterschießen ausgeschieden ist.
Im Elfmeterschießen ist die Mannschaft ausgeschieden worden.
questions.explanation: Headlines are short and leave out verbs and articles: "Aus im Elfmeterschießen" (out on penalties). The other versions are full sentences, wordy or (the last one) an incorrect passive of an intransitive verb.

questions.stem: Build the sentence from a match report.
questions.prompt: Cheered by the fans, the team left the pitch.
questions.explanation: The participle phrase "Von den Fans umjubelt" fills position 1 and is followed by a comma; the conjugated verb verließ comes next, then the subject die Mannschaft.

questions.stem: Read the cup report: "Lange lag Eichenried vorn. Erst in der 88. Minute glich Hollerbach durch einen Kopfball von Lenz aus. Im Elfmeterschießen hielt Torhüterin Kim zwei Schüsse, und Hollerbach zog ins Halbfinale ein." How did Hollerbach reach the semi-final?
choices: Lenz scored the winning goal in the 88th minute.
They equalized late and then won the penalty shoot-out.
An Eichenried player scored an own goal.
They won with a goal in extra time.
questions.explanation: "glich … aus" means Hollerbach equalized in the 88th minute; the match then went to a penalty shoot-out, in which goalkeeper Kim saved (hielt) two shots. Lenz's header was the equalizer, not a winner.

questions.stem: Complete: "Seit Montag ___ die Brücke gesperrt."
questions.explanation: "seit Montag" describes how things are now, a state, so it is the Zustandspassiv: sein + Partizip II, "ist gesperrt". "wird gesperrt" would describe the action of closing it, and with "seit" it would mean they keep closing it again and again. "wurde" needs a point in time (am Montag). The passive is never formed with "hat".

questions.stem: Complete the sign: "Achtung, die Fassade ___ gerade gestrichen!"
questions.explanation: "gerade" (right now) shows that the action is in progress, so you need the Vorgangspassiv with werden: "wird gerade gestrichen". "ist gestrichen" would mean the painting is already finished, which doesn't fit "gerade". "war" is past, and haben doesn't form the passive.

questions.stem: Which sentence describes a state, not an action?
choices: Die Straße wird um acht Uhr gesperrt.
Die Straße wurde von der Polizei gesperrt.
Die Straße ist seit gestern gesperrt.
questions.explanation: "ist seit gestern gesperrt" is the Zustandspassiv (sein + Partizip II with "seit"): the road is closed now. "wird um acht Uhr gesperrt" and "wurde von der Polizei gesperrt" are actions (a point in time, an agent with von), and "ist gesperrt worden" is the Perfekt of the Vorgangspassiv: the ending "worden" shows that it reports the action.

questions.stem: What is "Die Brücke ist eingestürzt."?
choices: the Zustandspassiv: someone has made the bridge collapse
the Perfekt of einstürzen: the bridge collapsed by itself
the Zustandspassiv of the verb stürzen
questions.explanation: einstürzen has no object and forms its Perfekt with sein, so "ist eingestürzt" is simply the active Perfekt: the bridge has collapsed. The present test shows it: "Die Brücke stürzt ein" (the bridge does it). A Zustandspassiv needs a verb that takes an object (sperren: Die Brücke ist gesperrt), and the Perfekt of the werden-passive would end in "worden".

questions.stem: The site manager says the scaffolding must be gone by Friday; he doesn't care when it is taken down. Which sentence says exactly that?
choices: Das Gerüst muss bis Freitag abgebaut werden.
Das Gerüst muss bis Freitag abgebaut haben.
Das Gerüst muss bis Freitag abgebaut worden.
Das Gerüst muss bis Freitag abgebaut sein.
questions.explanation: modal + Partizip II + sein is the Zustandspassiv with a modal: the state "taken down" must exist by Friday. "muss abgebaut werden" is also correct German, but it is about the action of taking it down. "abgebaut haben" is active (the scaffolding would do the dismantling), and "muss … abgebaut worden" lacks the final "sein".

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT natural German?
choices: Das Haus ist aus Holz gebaut.
Die Baustelle ist jeden Tag besucht.
Die Einfahrt ist schon wieder versperrt.
questions.explanation: Only verbs whose action leaves a lasting result have a Zustandspassiv. Visiting leaves nothing behind, so "Die Baustelle ist besucht" doesn't work; you need the Vorgangspassiv: "Die Baustelle wird jeden Tag besucht". Selling, building and blocking all produce a state (sold, built, blocked), so the other three are fine.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Die Straße ist gestern von der Polizei gesperrt.
Die Straße wurde gestern von der Polizei gesperrt.
Die Straße wird seit gestern von der Polizei gesperrt.
Die Straße ist gestern von der Polizei gesperrt geworden.
questions.explanation: An agent with von and a point in time (gestern) belong to the action, the Vorgangspassiv: "wurde gestern von der Polizei gesperrt". The Zustandspassiv describes a state, so "ist gestern … gesperrt" doesn't work with a point in time. "wird seit gestern" mixes an action with a state expression, and the passive participle of werden is "worden", not "geworden".

questions.stem: A news report says that the old cinema was demolished last week (reporting the action, in the Perfekt). Which sentence is right?
choices: Das alte Kino ist letzte Woche abgerissen.
Das alte Kino hat letzte Woche abgerissen worden.
Das alte Kino ist letzte Woche abgerissen worden.
Das alte Kino ist letzte Woche abgerissen geworden.
