questions.explanation: A plural noun without an article can't show the genitive, so it switches to the dative: "mittels Röntgenstrahlen". "Röntgenstrahls" is a genitive singular (one X-ray beam), "Röntgenstrahlens" doesn't exist, and "des" doesn't fit a plural.

questions.stem: Type the preposition: "Die Praxis liegt ___ des Bahnhofs." (not far from)
questions.explanation: "unweit" + genitive means "not far from": "unweit des Bahnhofs". In everyday German: "nicht weit vom Bahnhof".

questions.stem: Type the preposition that means "including": "Die Kosten ___ der Medikamente trägt die Krankenkasse."
questions.explanation: "einschließlich" + genitive means including: "einschließlich der Medikamente". "inklusive" means the same and is also correct. Don't confuse it with "ausschließlich" (exclusively, or excluding).

questions.stem: What does "Seitens der Klinik gab es keine Einwände." mean?
choices: There were no objections next to the hospital.
There were no objections about the hospital.
The hospital had no side entrances.
There were no objections on the part of the hospital.
questions.explanation: "seitens" + genitive names the side that does something: the hospital raised no objections. It's not about place ("next to") or topic ("about"), even though it contains the word "Seite".

questions.stem: Which sentence fits a postcard to a friend?
choices: Zwecks Erholung befinde ich mich am Meer.
Ich bin am Meer, um mich zu erholen.
Zwecks meiner Erholung erfolgt ein Aufenthalt am Meer.
Seitens meiner Person erfolgt Erholung am Meer.
questions.explanation: "zwecks" and "seitens" are office German and sound comic in a postcard. The natural personal version uses "um … zu". The other three are grammatical but sound like a form.

questions.stem: Match each formal preposition to its everyday alternative.
questions.explanation: "ungeachtet der Kritik" = "trotz der Kritik"; "seitens der Ärzte" = "von den Ärzten"; "mittels eines Tests" = "mit einem Test"; "inmitten der Stadt" = "mitten in der Stadt". None of them means "ohne".

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: Contrary to her doctor's advice, she went back to work.
questions.explanation: Entgegen dem Rat ihrer Ärztin ging sie wieder arbeiten. "entgegen" takes the dative (dem Rat), "ihrer Ärztin" is a genitive attribute (whose advice). When the whole phrase is position 1, the verb "ging" comes next, then the subject; it can also follow the verb: Sie ging entgegen dem Rat ihrer Ärztin wieder arbeiten.

questions.stem: Build the sentence.
questions.prompt: The pathogen was detected by means of a blood test.
questions.explanation: Der Erreger wurde mittels eines Bluttests nachgewiesen. "mittels" + genitive (eines Bluttests); the passive participle "nachgewiesen" goes to the end. The mittels phrase can also start the sentence: Mittels eines Bluttests wurde der Erreger nachgewiesen.

questions.stem: Complete: "Der kleine Eingriff wird ___ durchgeführt; Sie können am selben Tag nach Hause gehen."
questions.explanation: "ambulant" means outpatient: you go home the same day. "stationär" (inpatient) is the opposite; "akut" (acute) and "ansteckend" (contagious) describe illnesses, not how a procedure is done.

questions.stem: What is "der Erreger"?
choices: the pathogen that causes an illness
questions.explanation: "der Erreger" (from "erregen", to cause, arouse) is the virus, bacterium or other agent that causes a disease. The similar-looking "die Erregung" means excitement, which makes "the excitement before an operation" tempting.

questions.stem: Which verb takes "sein" in the perfect?
questions.explanation: "erkranken" describes a change of state (becoming ill) and has no object, so it takes "sein": "Sie ist an Grippe erkrankt." "diagnostizieren", "untersuchen" and "behandeln" take objects and use "haben".

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. Why is the appointment postponed?

audio.text: Guten Tag, hier ist die Praxis Doktor Lange. Ihr Termin am Donnerstag muss leider verschoben werden. Aufgrund einer Erkrankung der Ärztin ist die Praxis bis einschließlich Freitag geschlossen. Bitte rufen Sie uns ab Montag an, um einen neuen Termin zu vereinbaren.

questions.explanation: "Aufgrund einer Erkrankung der Ärztin": because the doctor is ill, the practice is closed up to and including Friday. The patient should call from Monday to make a new appointment.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio report. What have several hospitals done?

audio.text: Die Grippewelle hat ihren Höhepunkt erreicht. Mehrere Kliniken in der Region haben planbare Eingriffe verschoben, um Betten auf den Intensivstationen frei zu halten. Experten raten Menschen mit Vorerkrankungen, große Menschenmengen zu meiden.

choices: postponed procedures that can be planned
questions.explanation: "Mehrere Kliniken … haben planbare Eingriffe verschoben": they postponed plannable procedures to keep intensive care beds free. Intensive care units are being kept free, not closed.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the second speaker object to?

audio.text: Ich gehe morgen wieder arbeiten. — Entgegen dem Rat deines Arztes? Du bist doch noch ansteckend! — Ich setze mich ja allein ins Büro.

choices: that the first speaker wants to see a doctor
that the first speaker works in an open-plan office
that the first speaker wants to stay at home
that the first speaker is going back to work while still contagious
questions.explanation: "Entgegen dem Rat deines Arztes? Du bist doch noch ansteckend!": going to work against the doctor's advice while still contagious. The first speaker replies that he'll sit alone in the office, so he isn't staying at home.

questions.stem:
Read the letter from a health insurance fund.

"Sehr geehrter Herr Kowalski, wir haben Ihren Antrag auf Erstattung der Kosten für Ihre Physiotherapie geprüft. Wir übernehmen die Kosten in Höhe von 240 Euro abzüglich der gesetzlichen Zuzahlung von 34 Euro. Der Betrag wird Ihnen innerhalb von zwei Wochen überwiesen. Zwecks Prüfung künftiger Behandlungen bitten wir Sie, uns die ärztliche Verordnung vor Beginn der Therapie zuzusenden."

How much money will Mr Kowalski receive?
questions.explanation: "abzüglich" means minus: 240 euros minus the 34-euro co-payment = 206 euros. 274 would be "zuzüglich" (plus); 34 euros is the part he has to pay himself.

questions.stem: Find the mistake: "Zwecks einem Gespräch bitten wir um Ihren Rückruf."
questions.explanation: "zwecks" is a genitive preposition, and with an article the genitive must show: "zwecks eines Gesprächs". "um Ihren Rückruf" is a correct accusative after "bitten um", and "wir bitten" agrees with "wir".

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Kollegin, ___ Mann Elternzeit nimmt, arbeitet Vollzeit."
questions.explanation: "whose" agrees with the owner, "die Kollegin" (feminine): "deren". It doesn't matter that "Mann" is masculine; "dessen" would be for a masculine or neuter owner. "derer" means "of those", and "die" would need a different clause.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das Dorf, ___ Bevölkerung schrumpft, sucht junge Familien."
questions.explanation: The owner is "das Dorf" (neuter), so "whose" is "dessen", even though "Bevölkerung" is feminine. "deren" would agree with "Bevölkerung", the classic mistake of looking forward instead of back.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das ist die Stiftung, mit ___ Hilfe das Haus gebaut wurde."
questions.explanation: "with whose help": the owner of the help is "die Stiftung" (feminine), so "deren". The preposition "mit" gives the dative to "Hilfe", but "deren" itself never changes. "der" would mean "with which" and leave "Hilfe" without an article.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Frau, mit deren ___ Tochter ich befreundet bin, wohnt nebenan."
questions.explanation: After "dessen/deren", adjectives take strong endings, as if there were no article: dative feminine "jüngster Tochter". "jüngsten" is the weak ending you'd use after "ihrer" (mit ihrer jüngsten Tochter), which is why it is tempting.

questions.stem: Type the relative pronoun: "Der Nachbar, ___ Kinder bei uns spielen, ist alleinerziehend."
questions.explanation: The owner is "der Nachbar" (masculine), so "whose" is "dessen". "Kinder" (plural) doesn't change it, and no article follows "dessen".

questions.stem: Complete the proverb: "Wer zu spät kommt, ___ bestraft das Leben."
questions.explanation: The pick-up word takes the case of the main clause: "das Leben" is the subject of "bestraft", and the person punished is the accusative object: "den". "der" would make the person the subject (who punishes life).

questions.stem: Complete: "Wem die Kinderbetreuung zu teuer ist, ___ kann einen Zuschuss beantragen."
questions.explanation: "wem" is dative in the relative clause, but in the main clause the person is the subject of "kann": nominative "der". "dem" repeats the case of the free relative instead of the main clause.

questions.stem: In which sentence could the pick-up word be left out?
choices: Wer zu spät kommt, den bestraft das Leben.
Wem das nicht gefällt, der kann gehen.
Wen das interessiert, dem empfehle ich den Bericht.
Wer A sagt, der muss auch B sagen.
questions.explanation: The pick-up word can only be dropped when it has the same case as the wh-word: "wer … der" (both nominative): "Wer A sagt, muss auch B sagen." In the other three the cases differ (nominative/accusative, dative/nominative, accusative/dative), so the pick-up word is needed.

questions.stem: What does "Die Zahl derer, die allein leben, steigt." mean?
choices: The number of those who live alone is rising.
The number of their children who live alone is rising.
Their number is rising because they live alone.
The number of people who live with them is rising.
questions.explanation: "derer" is the genitive plural of the demonstrative "die" (those) before a relative clause: "the number of those who live alone". It isn't a possessive like "deren" (their/whose).

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a formal relative pronoun to avoid "die die"?
choices: Die Forscherin, die die Studie leitet, ist Demografin.
Die Forscherin, welche die Studie leitet, ist Demografin.
Die Forscherin, deren die Studie leitet, ist Demografin.
Die Forscherin, welches die Studie leitet, ist Demografin.
questions.explanation: "welche" (feminine, nominative) replaces "die" as a formal relative pronoun, avoiding "die die". The sentence with "die die" is correct but has the repetition; "deren" means "whose"; "welches" is neuter and doesn't agree with "Forscherin".

questions.stem: Build the sentence, starting with "Das ist".
questions.prompt: That's the woman whose eldest son lives in Canada.
questions.explanation: Das ist die Frau, deren ältester Sohn in Kanada lebt. "deren" agrees with "die Frau"; the adjective after "deren" takes the strong ending (masculine nominative -er: "ältester"); the verb goes to the end of the relative clause.

questions.stem: Build the proverb, starting with "Wer".
questions.prompt: Whoever comes too late is punished by life.
questions.explanation: Wer zu spät kommt, den bestraft das Leben. The free relative clause comes first, with its verb at the end. The pick-up word "den" (accusative, the person punished) opens the main clause, then the verb, then the subject "das Leben".

questions.stem: Which participle attribute means the same as "die Menschen, die allein leben"?
questions.explanation: "leben" is an active, ongoing action without an object, so Partizip I: "die allein lebenden Menschen". "gelebt" can't be used as an attribute for people here (leben takes haben and no object); "zu lebend" would add "must".

questions.stem: Which relative clause can NOT be turned into a participle attribute?
choices: die Kinder, die im letzten Jahr geboren wurden
die Stadt, in der ich wohne
ein Programm, das vom Bund gefördert wird
questions.explanation: Only a relative pronoun that is the subject can disappear into an attribute. In "die Stadt, in der ich wohne" the relative pronoun is part of a prepositional phrase and "ich" is the subject, so there is no attribute version. The others become "die im letzten Jahr geborenen Kinder", "ein vom Bund gefördertes Programm" and "die allein lebenden Menschen".

questions.stem: Complete: "Viele Eltern wünschen sich eine bessere ___ von Familie und Beruf."
questions.explanation: "die Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf" is the fixed phrase for reconciling family and work. "Elternzeit" is parental leave, which doesn't fit "von Familie und Beruf"; "Lebensform" and "Abwanderung" don't make sense here.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the correct perfect of "sich scheiden lassen"?
questions.explanation: "lassen" with another infinitive forms its perfect with "haben" and the infinitive "lassen" instead of a participle: "Sie haben sich scheiden lassen." "sind" is the wrong auxiliary, the reflexive "sich" can't be left out, and "geschieden" belongs to the state "Sie sind geschieden".

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. Why did the population grow?

audio.text: Nach neuen Zahlen des Landesamts für Statistik ist die Zahl der Geburten im vergangenen Jahr erneut zurückgegangen. Trotzdem ist die Bevölkerung leicht gewachsen, und zwar vor allem durch Zuwanderung.

questions.explanation: "vor allem durch Zuwanderung": mainly through immigration. The number of births fell again ("ist … zurückgegangen"), so births can't explain the growth; life expectancy and people moving away aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen to Jana's voicemail. What does she ask her father to do?

audio.text: Hallo Papa, hier ist Jana. Kannst du am Mittwoch die Kinder von der Kita abholen? Die Kinderbetreuung schließt diese Woche schon um drei, und ich habe bis fünf eine Besprechung. Ruf mich kurz an, ob das klappt.

choices: look after the children all week
go to a meeting for her
pick the children up from nursery on Wednesday
questions.explanation: "Kannst du am Mittwoch die Kinder von der Kita abholen?": pick them up on Wednesday, because the childcare closes at three and she has a meeting until five. She asks him to call her, not the nursery.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the second speaker say?

audio.text: Das Mehrgenerationenhaus ist doch nur etwas für Rentner. — Überhaupt nicht! Wer dort einmal einen Nachmittag verbracht hat, der weiß, wie viele junge Familien hinkommen.

choices: Many young families go there too.
questions.explanation: She contradicts the first speaker ("Überhaupt nicht!") and says that anyone who has spent an afternoon there knows how many young families come. Note the free relative clause "Wer …, der weiß …".

questions.stem:
Read the forum post.

"Unser Dorf hat ein Problem, dessen Folgen man überall sieht: Die jungen Leute ziehen weg, die Schule hat nur noch zwei Klassen, und der letzte Laden, dessen Besitzerin achtzig ist, schließt im Sommer. Wer hier bleibt, ist meistens über sechzig. Trotzdem gibt es Hoffnung. Im letzten Jahr sind fünf Familien zu uns gezogen, deren Kinder in der Stadt keinen Kitaplatz gefunden hatten. Was sie mitgebracht haben, ist vor allem eines: neue Ideen."

Why did the families move to the village?
choices: They found jobs in the village shop.
Their children hadn't found a nursery place in the city.
They wanted to open a new school.
questions.explanation: "fünf Familien …, deren Kinder in der Stadt keinen Kitaplatz gefunden hatten": their children had no nursery place in the city. The shop is closing, and no school plans or inheritances are mentioned.

questions.stem: What does the present tense in "Eine Zensur findet nicht statt." (Art. 5 GG) express?
choices: a description: there happens to be no censorship at the moment
a question about whether there is censorship
a prediction: there will be no censorship
a ban: censorship is not allowed
questions.explanation: In laws the present tense is normative: it says what must (or must not) be the case. "Eine Zensur findet nicht statt" forbids censorship; it doesn't report on the current situation or predict the future.

questions.stem: What does "Über die Zulässigkeit und Fortdauer einer Freiheitsentziehung hat nur der Richter zu entscheiden." (Art. 104 Abs. 2 GG) mean?
choices: Only a judge may decide whether, and for how long, someone is deprived of liberty.
The judge has decided on depriving someone of liberty.
The judge must be deprived of liberty.
Only the judge is free to decide anything.
questions.explanation: "haben + zu" expresses a duty or competence: only the judge has to (and may) decide. "hat entschieden" would be the perfect; "Freiheitsentziehung" is the deprivation of liberty, not the judge's own.

questions.stem: In "Jeder … vorläufig Festgenommene ist spätestens am Tage nach der Festnahme dem Richter vorzuführen, …" (Art. 104 Abs. 3 GG), what does "ist … vorzuführen" mean?
choices: wants to be brought before (a judge)
questions.explanation: "sein + zu" is a passive with a modal meaning, in laws usually "must": "muss vorgeführt werden". It isn't past, active or about wishes.

questions.stem: How do you read "Art. 5 Abs. 1 S. 3 GG" aloud?
choices: Artikel fünf, Abschnitt eins, Seite drei
Artikel fünf, Absatz eins, Satz drei Grundgesetz
Absatz fünf, Artikel eins, Satz drei Grundgesetz
Artikel fünf, Absatz eins, Stelle drei Grundgesetz
questions.explanation: "Art." = Artikel, "Abs." = Absatz (paragraph), "S." = Satz (sentence), "GG" = Grundgesetz. "S." in a legal citation is never "Seite" (page), and the order goes from the largest unit to the smallest.

questions.stem: Art. 20 says: "Alle Staatsgewalt geht vom Volke aus." How would you write "vom Volke" in modern German?
questions.explanation: The dative -e on masculine and neuter nouns (dem Volke, im Falle, dem Schutze) is old-fashioned. Today: "vom Volk". Recognize the old form, but don't use it in your own writing.

questions.stem: Which word means "unconstitutional"?
questions.explanation: "verfassungswidrig" = against ("wider") the constitution ("Verfassung"). "unantastbar" means inviolable, "verankert" anchored or laid down, and "rechtsstaatlich" in line with the rule of law, almost the opposite.

questions.stem: Art. 8 begins "Alle Deutschen haben das Recht, sich … zu versammeln". What does the wording "Alle Deutschen" tell you?
choices: Germans are obliged to attend assemblies.
The article gives this right to German citizens.
The right applies only to Germans living abroad.
questions.explanation: Some basic rights begin with "Jeder" or "Alle Menschen" (rights of everyone), others with "Alle Deutschen" (rights of citizens, the "Deutschenrechte"). A right is not a duty, and paragraph 1 itself says "ohne Anmeldung oder Erlaubnis" (paragraph 2 lets laws regulate open-air assemblies).

questions.stem: Which is the best paraphrase of "Die Wohnung ist unverletzlich." (Art. 13)?
choices: Flats may not be damaged by their tenants.
Nobody may be injured at home.
The state may not simply enter or search a person's home.
Everyone has a right to a flat.
questions.explanation: "unverletzlich" here means protected from intrusion: the article protects the home against the state, which may only search it under strict conditions. It isn't about damage, injuries or a right to housing.

questions.stem: Art. 79 protects "die in den Artikeln 1 und 20 niedergelegten Grundsätze". What does "niedergelegt" mean here?
questions.explanation: "niederlegen" has several meanings; in a text about principles in articles it means to lay down in writing: the principles set out in Articles 1 and 20. "ein Amt niederlegen" (to resign) is another meaning that doesn't fit principles. The phrase is an extended participle attribute: "die Grundsätze, die in den Artikeln 1 und 20 niedergelegt sind".

questions.stem: Listen to the news item. What must the state parliament do?

audio.text: Das Verfassungsgericht des Landes hat heute entschieden, dass Teile des neuen Versammlungsgesetzes verfassungswidrig sind. Nach Ansicht der Richterinnen und Richter schränken die Regeln die Versammlungsfreiheit zu stark ein. Der Landtag muss das Gesetz bis zum Ende des Jahres ändern.

choices: change the law by the end of the year
questions.explanation: "Der Landtag muss das Gesetz bis zum Ende des Jahres ändern": the state parliament must change the law, because parts of it restrict freedom of assembly too much and are unconstitutional.

questions.stem: Listen to the lecture extract. What do the courts do, according to the speaker?

audio.text: Die Gewaltenteilung bedeutet, dass die Macht im Staat auf drei Bereiche verteilt ist. Das Parlament macht die Gesetze, die Regierung und die Verwaltung führen sie aus, und die Gerichte kontrollieren, ob sie eingehalten werden.

choices: check whether the laws are kept
questions.explanation: "die Gerichte kontrollieren, ob sie eingehalten werden": the courts check that the laws are kept. Parliament makes them, and the government and administration carry them out.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: state under the rule of law
questions.explanation: das Grundrecht = basic right (Articles 1 to 19 of the Grundgesetz); die Gewaltenteilung = separation of powers; der Rechtsstaat = a state bound by law; die Würde = dignity (Art. 1). Freedom of the press is "die Pressefreiheit".

questions.stem: Which intensifier suggests that a "but" is probably coming? "Der Film ist ___ gelungen, …"
questions.explanation: "durchaus" concedes a point ("certainly, definitely") and often prepares a criticism: "durchaus gelungen, aber zu lang". "äußerst", "überaus" and "höchst" simply make the praise stronger.

questions.stem: What does "Der Roman ist alles andere als langweilig." mean?
choices: Everything except the novel is boring.
The novel is a bit boring.
The novel is anything but boring.
questions.explanation: "alles andere als" = anything but: the novel is not boring at all. It's a common way to praise by denying the negative. It doesn't compare the novel with other things.

questions.stem: Which phrase sounds natural in a review?
questions.explanation: "etwas" (a bit) goes mostly with negative adjectives: "etwas langatmig". "etwas spannend" sounds odd (use "recht" or "ziemlich spannend"), "höchst" doesn't combine with simple "gut", and "überaus okay" mixes a formal intensifier with a colloquial word.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the usual way to summarize the plot in a German review?
choices: Nora kehrt in ihr Heimatdorf zurück.
Nora kehrte in ihr Heimatdorf zurück.
Nora war in ihr Heimatdorf zurückgekehrt.
Nora wird in ihr Heimatdorf zurückkehren.
questions.explanation: Plot summaries in reviews and Inhaltsangaben use the present tense. The Präteritum is the tense of the novel itself, not of the review; the Plusquamperfekt and future would be odd for the main events.

questions.stem: A critic writes: "Etwas mehr Tempo hätte dem Film gutgetan." What does the critic think?
choices: The film should have had more pace.
The film will be faster in the director's cut.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv II of the past ("hätte gutgetan") describes something that didn't happen: more pace would have done the film good, so it was too slow. It's a polite way to criticize.

questions.stem: Which adjective is the opposite of "gelungen"?
questions.explanation: "gelungen" (from gelingen) means successful; "misslungen" (from misslingen) means failed. "fesselnd" and "lesenswert" are positive too, and "gelingend" isn't used as an adjective.

questions.stem: Complete with a participle attribute: "die Kommissarin, die von Lena Hartmann gespielt wird" → "die von Lena Hartmann ___ Kommissarin"
questions.explanation: A passive relative clause becomes a Partizip II attribute; after "die" in the feminine singular nominative the ending is -e: "die von Lena Hartmann gespielte Kommissarin".

questions.stem: What is "die Uraufführung"?
choices: the very first performance of a new work
the last performance of a season
a performance in the original language
questions.explanation: "Ur-" means original or first: "die Uraufführung" is the world premiere of a new play, opera or piece of music. A performance in the original language is "in Originalsprache"; a costume rehearsal is "die Generalprobe".

questions.stem: In which part of a German newspaper do you find reviews of books and plays?
questions.explanation: "das Feuilleton" is the arts and culture section. The "Leitartikel" is the editorial, an opinion piece on a news topic; business and sport have their own sections.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker criticize?

audio.text: Ich habe mir gestern die neue Verfilmung angesehen. Die Besetzung ist wirklich gut, aber die Geschichte zieht sich. Nach einer Stunde habe ich ehrlich gesagt auf die Uhr geschaut.

questions.explanation: "die Geschichte zieht sich" (the story drags), and after an hour the speaker was looking at the clock. The cast is praised ("wirklich gut"); the cinema and the ending aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen. What did the second speaker do?

audio.text: Das Buch ist so packend, ich habe es an einem Wochenende gelesen. — Wirklich? Ich fand den Anfang ziemlich langatmig und habe nach fünfzig Seiten aufgehört.

choices: read the book in one weekend
recommended the book to a friend
questions.explanation: The second speaker found the beginning "ziemlich langatmig" and stopped after fifty pages. Reading it in one weekend is what the first speaker did.

questions.stem: Put the parts of a review in the usual order.
choices: Introduction: title, author or director, genre
Short summary of the content, without the ending
questions.explanation: A review first introduces the work, then summarizes it (present tense, no spoilers), then judges it with reasons, and ends with a conclusion and a recommendation for a particular audience.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a modal particle correctly to turn "Komm rein" into a warm invitation?
questions.explanation: A modal particle goes in the middle of the sentence, after the verb (and after any pronouns): "Komm doch rein!" It can never stand first ("Doch komm rein" reads as "But come in") or be tacked on at the end.

questions.stem: Complete with the particle that marks something both speakers already know: "Du kennst ___ meine Schwester, sie ist sehr direkt."
questions.explanation: In a statement, "ja" means "as you know, as we both know": you know my sister, after all. "denn" as a particle only appears in questions, "etwa" in surprised yes/no questions, and "mal" softens requests, not statements of fact.

questions.stem: Which question sounds natural and shows friendly interest?
questions.explanation: "denn" in a question signals interest. Like all particles it comes after the verb and after the pronouns: "Wie geht es dir denn?" Putting it before the pronouns ("geht denn es dir") or in position 1 is wrong.

questions.stem: "Hast du etwa schon gegessen?" What does the speaker feel?
choices: They want to know roughly when you ate.
Surprise: they expect, or hope, that the answer is no.
They are inviting you to eat with them.
They are certain that you have eaten.
questions.explanation: "etwa" in a yes/no question shows surprise and an expectation of "no": surely you haven't eaten already? It is tempting to read it as "about, approximately", but that is the adverb, used with numbers (etwa zwanzig Leute).

questions.stem: Your colleague complains that the old printer has broken down again. Which reply means "that's just how it is"?
questions.explanation: "halt" (like "eben") expresses resignation: it's old, there's nothing to be done. The questions with "etwa" and "denn" ask something instead of accepting it, and "ruhig" gives permission, which makes no sense here.

questions.stem: What does "Sie können mich ruhig unterbrechen." mean?
questions.explanation: As a particle with können or an imperative, "ruhig" gives permission or encouragement: go ahead. The adjective ruhig ("quiet, calm") tempts the translation "quietly", but in this position it is the particle.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a warning?
choices: Erzähl das bloß nicht deinem Chef!
questions.explanation: "bloß" (or "nur") in an imperative turns it into a warning: whatever you do, don't tell your boss! "doch" urges you to tell him, "mal" makes it a casual suggestion, and "ruhig" says it's fine to tell him.

questions.stem: Which sentence has the modal particle in a correct position?
choices: Ich habe doch es dir gestern gesagt.
Ich doch habe es dir gestern gesagt.
Ich habe es dir doch gestern gesagt.
Ich habe es dir gestern gesagt, doch.
questions.explanation: The particle goes after the pronouns (es dir) and before the new information: "Ich habe es dir doch gestern gesagt." Before the pronouns ("doch es dir") sounds wrong, and a particle can neither come before the verb nor be added at the end.

questions.stem: In which sentence is "schon" a modal particle, not "already"?
choices: Ich war schon dreimal in Wien.
Keine Sorge, das wird schon klappen.
Er ist schon um sechs gegangen.
questions.explanation: In "Das wird schon klappen" schon reassures: it'll work out, don't worry. In the other sentences it has its time meaning "already" (fertig already, three times already, gone already at six).

questions.stem: Someone says "Er ist EBEN gegangen", with clear stress on "eben". What does it mean?
choices: He left just now, a moment ago.
That's just how it is: he left.
questions.explanation: Stressed, "eben" is the time adverb "just now". The unstressed modal particle eben would mean "well, he left, that's how it is". Stress is one of the clearest ways to tell a particle from the same word with its ordinary meaning.

questions.stem: At a party you have been chatting about the weather. Which question moves to a new topic naturally?
questions.explanation: "eigentlich" in a question opens a new topic, like "by the way" or "actually": what do you actually do for a living? "etwa" only works in yes/no questions with surprise, and "ruhig" and "halt" don't belong in this kind of question.

questions.stem: Match each particle to what it usually does.
choices: makes a request casual and softer
questions.explanation: ja = as we know; denn = interest in questions; mal = softening; wohl = I suppose, probably; etwa = surely not …? Giving permission is the job of ruhig, which isn't in the list.

questions.stem: Make this request softer and more casual with one modal particle: "Kannst du ___ kurz helfen?"
questions.explanation: "Kannst du mal kurz helfen?" is the most natural choice: mal makes the request sound small and casual. "eben" (northern) and "vielleicht" (which also works as a softening particle) are accepted too. "doch" doesn't work in a question like this, and "denn" would show interest rather than soften.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker express?

audio.text: Mensch, du bist ja ganz nass! Hast du etwa keinen Schirm dabei?

choices: A reminder: they had told you to take an umbrella.
Surprise: they have just noticed you are wet, and they suspect you have no umbrella.
Permission: you may borrow their umbrella.
A warning: don't get wet again.
questions.explanation: "Du bist ja ganz nass!" is ja in an exclamation: surprise at what you've just noticed. "Hast du etwa keinen Schirm dabei?" uses etwa: a surprised question (surely you haven't come without an umbrella?). There is no reminder (that would be doch), no permission (ruhig) and no warning (bloß).

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. Which statement is true?

audio.text: Hallo Tom, hier ist Lena. Du, ich weiß ja, dass du am Samstag eigentlich keine Zeit hast. Aber komm doch wenigstens kurz vorbei, man wird halt nur einmal dreißig! Ruf mich mal an.

choices: Lena is cancelling her birthday party.
Lena knows Tom is busy on Saturday, but urges him to drop by briefly.
Lena asks Tom to bring something to eat.
Lena is annoyed that Tom never calls her.
questions.explanation: Lena says "ich weiß ja, dass du am Samstag eigentlich keine Zeit hast" (as we both know, you're actually busy) and then "komm doch wenigstens kurz vorbei" (do drop by at least briefly): doch urges. "Ruf mich mal an" is a casual request, not a complaint.

questions.stem: Listen to the two colleagues. What does the second speaker advise?

audio.text: Der Chef hat schon wieder die Pointe vergessen. — Na ja, er ist eben kein Komiker. Lach einfach trotzdem.

choices: To remind the boss of the punchline.
questions.explanation: The second speaker says "Na ja, er ist eben kein Komiker. Lach einfach trotzdem.": he simply isn't a comedian (eben: that's how it is), so just laugh anyway. Nobody suggests telling the boss the punchline.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: Do sit down for a moment!
questions.explanation: "Setz dich doch mal kurz!": the imperative first, then the pronoun dich, then the particles in their usual order (doch before mal), then kurz. "denn" doesn't belong in an imperative.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: You can't be serious!
questions.explanation: "Das ist ja wohl nicht dein Ernst!": the combination ja wohl expresses indignation, and both particles come before nicht. "etwa" is used in questions, not in this exclamation.

questions.stem: Read: "Viele Austauschstudierende sind am Anfang überrascht, wie direkt Deutsche sein können. Wenn ein Kollege sagt: 'Dein Vortrag war zu lang', meint er das meistens nicht unhöflich, sondern sachlich. Smalltalk über das Wetter oder das Wochenende gibt es zwar auch, aber er dauert oft nicht so lange wie in anderen Ländern. Wer taktvoll sein will, kann Kritik mit Modalpartikeln weicher machen: 'Vielleicht könntest du den Vortrag mal etwas kürzen?' klingt viel freundlicher." According to the text, how can you make criticism softer?
choices: By using modal particles, for example in a polite question.
By making more small talk first.
questions.explanation: The last sentence says that someone who wants to be tactful can soften criticism with modal particles, and gives the example with vielleicht and mal. Small talk is mentioned, but not as a way to soften criticism, and the text says directness is usually meant sachlich, not that you should always be direct.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Frag ruhig, wenn du etwas nicht verstehst.
Das war doch nur ein Witz!
questions.explanation: As a modal particle, "denn" only appears in questions ("Was ist denn hier los?"). In a statement it can only be the conjunction "because", which needs a clause after it. The other three use their particles correctly: ruhig for permission, doch for a reminder.

questions.stem: Complete so that the clause says how (by what means): "Man kann Stress abbauen, ___ man regelmäßig Sport treibt."
questions.explanation: "indem" gives the means: you reduce stress by doing sport. "damit" would give a purpose (so that), "sofern" a condition (provided that) and "ohne dass" the opposite (without anyone doing sport).

questions.stem: Which clause is correct?
questions.explanation: indem is a subordinating conjunction: subject after it, conjugated verb at the end ("treibt"). Keeping the verb in second position is main-clause order, the most common learner mistake with new conjunctions.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Sie hat ihre Angst überwunden, indem sie jeden Tag geübt hat."?
choices: Sie hat ihre Angst überwunden, damit sie jeden Tag geübt hat.
Sie hat ihre Angst überwunden, obwohl sie jeden Tag geübt hat.
Sie hat ihre Angst überwunden, ohne jeden Tag zu üben.
Sie hat ihre Angst dadurch überwunden, dass sie jeden Tag geübt hat.
questions.explanation: dadurch (in the main clause) + dass expresses the same means as indem, with a little more emphasis. damit is purpose, obwohl concession, and ohne … zu says she didn't practise, the opposite.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ ich weiß, ist die Beratung an der Uni kostenlos."
questions.explanation: "Soweit ich weiß" = as far as I know, and the conjunction is one word. "so weit" in two words is the adverb phrase ("Es ist so weit"). "Insofern" usually points to an als clause (in that) and isn't used for "as far as I know", and "indem" (by doing) makes no sense here.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Je nachdem, wie ich mich fühle, ich gehe abends joggen.
Je nachdem, wie ich mich fühle, gehe ich abends joggen.
Je nachdem, wie fühle ich mich, gehe ich abends joggen.
Je nachdem wie ich fühle mich, gehe ich abends joggen.
questions.explanation: The indirect question after je nachdem has its verb at the end ("wie ich mich fühle"), and the whole je nachdem part fills position 1, so the main verb comes straight after it: "gehe ich". Starting the main clause with "ich" ignores that the first position is already taken.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich gehe jeden Abend spazieren, es sei denn, ___."
questions.explanation: After "es sei denn" a clause in main-clause order follows: "es sei denn, es regnet" (unless it rains). "regnet es" has the verb first, "es regnen" isn't conjugated, and "dass es nicht regnet" would give the opposite meaning: unless it doesn't rain.

questions.stem: Complete: "Er verließ die Sitzung, ___ es jemand bemerkte."
questions.explanation: The two clauses have different subjects (er … jemand), so you need "ohne dass" + verb at the end: he left without anyone noticing. "ohne … zu" needs the same subject and an infinitive, and "statt" (instead of) doesn't fit the meaning.

questions.stem: Complete: "Er verließ die Sitzung, ___ sich zu verabschieden."
questions.explanation: Same subject (he left, he didn't say goodbye) and a zu-infinitive: "ohne sich zu verabschieden". "ohne dass" would need a full clause with a conjugated verb, and "indem" would mean he left by saying goodbye.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Das Thema ist zu komplex, dass man es in einer Stunde behandeln könnte.
Das Thema ist so komplex, als dass man es in einer Stunde behandeln könnte.
Das Thema ist zu komplex, als dass man es in einer Stunde behandeln könnte.
Das Thema ist zu komplex, als dass man könnte es in einer Stunde behandeln.
questions.explanation: The pattern is zu + adjective, als dass + verb at the end, usually in the Konjunktiv II: "zu komplex, als dass man es … behandeln könnte". "dass" alone is missing als, "so … als dass" mixes two patterns (so … dass would be "so … that"), and the last sentence has the verb in the wrong place.

questions.stem: What does "Er hat insofern recht, als Sport allein keine Depression heilt." mean?
choices: He is right in that exercise alone doesn't cure depression.
He is right, provided that exercise cures depression.
He is right because he does a lot of exercise.
He is only right if he exercises.
questions.explanation: insofern …, als = in that, to the extent that: the als clause gives the respect in which he is right. It's tempting to read insofern like sofern (provided that), but sofern would need a condition, and the sentence states a fact.

questions.stem: "Sofern nichts dazwischenkommt, beginnt der Kurs im März." Which sentence is closest in meaning?
choices: Obwohl nichts dazwischenkommt, beginnt der Kurs im März.
Weil nichts dazwischenkommt, beginnt der Kurs im März.
Damit nichts dazwischenkommt, beginnt der Kurs im März.
Wenn nichts dazwischenkommt, beginnt der Kurs im März.
questions.explanation: sofern states a condition, like wenn or falls but a little more formal: provided nothing gets in the way. obwohl is a concession, weil a reason and damit a purpose.

questions.stem: Match each connector to its meaning.
questions.explanation: indem gives the means, sofern a condition, soweit a limit (soweit ich weiß), je nachdem a dependency, and außer wenn an exception. "although" would be obwohl or wenngleich (lesson 18).

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Wir treffen uns drinnen oder draußen, je ___, ob es regnet."
questions.explanation: "je nachdem, ob …" = depending on whether. Note the comma after je nachdem and the verb at the end of the ob clause.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Statt ___ ihr Chef sie entlastet, gibt er ihr noch mehr Arbeit."
questions.explanation: The two clauses have different subjects (ihr Chef … er gibt ihr), so it is "statt dass" + verb at the end. With the same subject you would use statt … zu: "Statt sich auszuruhen, arbeitet sie weiter."

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: You can reduce stress by taking breaks.
questions.explanation: Main clause with the modal verb in position 2 and the infinitive at the end (kann … abbauen), then the indem clause with its verb at the end (indem man Pausen macht). "damit" would express a purpose, not the means.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: Depending on what the weather is like, we'll meet outside.
questions.explanation: "Je nachdem, wie das Wetter ist" is the first element; its verb (ist) goes to the end. Because it fills position 1, the main verb follows immediately: "treffen wir uns draußen". "ob" would need a yes/no question ("ob es regnet"), which doesn't fit "das Wetter ist".

questions.stem: Listen to the lecture extract. Which statement matches it?

audio.text: Resilienz ist keine angeborene Eigenschaft. Man kann sie stärken, indem man lernt, Probleme als lösbar wahrzunehmen. Allerdings ersetzt ein solches Training keine Therapie, sofern eine psychische Erkrankung vorliegt.

choices: Resilience is something you are born with or not.
Resilience training is no substitute for therapy if there is a mental illness.
Therapy is only necessary if resilience training fails.
You become resilient by ignoring problems.
questions.explanation: The speaker says resilience isn't innate ("keine angeborene Eigenschaft"), that you strengthen it by learning to see problems as solvable, and that training doesn't replace therapy "sofern eine psychische Erkrankung vorliegt", provided (if) there is a mental illness. Nothing is said about therapy only after training fails.

questions.stem: Listen to the voicemail. When will Mr Brandt not come to the workshop?

audio.text: Hallo Frau Weber, hier ist Jonas Brandt. Ich komme morgen gern zum Workshop, es sei denn, mein Sohn ist noch krank. Dann würde ich Ihnen bis acht Uhr Bescheid geben.

choices: If the workshop starts before eight.
If his son is still ill.
If Ms Weber doesn't call him back.
If his son wants to come along.
questions.explanation: "Ich komme morgen gern zum Workshop, es sei denn, mein Sohn ist noch krank": es sei denn = unless. Eight o'clock is the time by which he would let her know, not the start of the workshop.

questions.stem: Listen. How did the second speaker stop smoking?

audio.text: Wie hast du es eigentlich geschafft, mit dem Rauchen aufzuhören? — Indem ich jedes Mal, wenn ich Lust auf eine Zigarette hatte, zehn Minuten spazieren gegangen bin.

choices: By smoking only after a ten-minute walk.
By walking to the shop instead of driving.
By seeing a doctor every ten days.
By going for a ten-minute walk whenever they wanted a cigarette.
questions.explanation: The answer starts with "Indem …", the means: whenever I felt like a cigarette, I went for a walk for ten minutes. The walk replaced the cigarette; it wasn't a condition for smoking.

questions.stem: Read the advice column: "Leserfrage: Ich grüble abends ständig über die Arbeit nach und kann dann nicht einschlafen. Was hilft? Antwort: Viele Menschen kennen das. Hilfreich ist es oft, den Tag bewusst abzuschließen, indem man seine Gedanken kurz aufschreibt. So muss man sie nicht im Kopf behalten. Auch feste Rituale am Abend können helfen, sofern man sie jeden Tag wiederholt. Wenn die Schlafprobleme jedoch über Wochen anhalten, sollte man ärztlichen Rat suchen, statt allein weiterzugrübeln." According to the answer, when should the reader see a doctor?
choices: If the sleeping problems last for weeks.
If writing down their thoughts doesn't help the first time.
If they don't have any evening rituals.
questions.explanation: The last sentence: "Wenn die Schlafprobleme jedoch über Wochen anhalten, sollte man ärztlichen Rat suchen". Writing down thoughts (indem …) and rituals (sofern man sie jeden Tag wiederholt) are the first suggestions, not reasons to see a doctor.

questions.stem: Which connector is formal and means "although"?
questions.explanation: wenngleich (like obgleich) is a formal obwohl, with the verb at the end. während means "while, whereas" (contrast), als ob "as if", and dagegen "by contrast".

questions.stem: Complete with the connector for a hypothetical extreme case ("even if"): "___ die Quote morgen abgeschafft würde, würde sich die Unternehmenskultur nicht sofort ändern."
questions.explanation: selbst wenn = even if, usually hypothetical, here with the Konjunktiv II (würde abgeschafft). obwohl is for real facts ("although it is abolished"), während is time or contrast, and als ob introduces an unreal comparison.

questions.stem: What does "Die Situation hat sich verbessert, wenn auch nur langsam." mean?
choices: The situation will improve if it happens slowly.
The situation only improves when people are slow.
The situation hasn't improved, although it was slow.
The situation has improved, albeit only slowly.
questions.explanation: wenn auch without a verb limits what was just said: albeit, though. Reading it as a condition (wenn = if) is the tempting mistake, but with auch and no verb it is concessive.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Sosehr ich mich bemühe auch, ich verstehe seine Haltung nicht.
Sosehr ich mich auch bemühe, ich verstehe seine Haltung nicht.
Sosehr bemühe ich mich auch, ich verstehe seine Haltung nicht.
Sosehr auch ich bemühe mich, ich verstehe seine Haltung nicht.
questions.explanation: In the "sosehr … auch" clause the verb goes to the end and auch stays in the middle: "Sosehr ich mich auch bemühe". The main clause may then begin with its own subject ("ich verstehe …"). The other versions put the verb in the wrong place or auch after the verb.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Er arbeitet Vollzeit, sie dagegen Teilzeit arbeitet.
Er arbeitet Vollzeit, sie dagegen arbeitet Teilzeit.
Er arbeitet Vollzeit, dagegen sie arbeitet Teilzeit.
Er arbeitet Vollzeit, während sie arbeitet Teilzeit.
questions.explanation: dagegen is an adverb, so it doesn't send the verb to the end. It can follow the subject it contrasts ("sie dagegen arbeitet") or stand in position 1 with inversion ("dagegen arbeitet sie"). "dagegen sie arbeitet" breaks verb-second, and after während (a conjunction) the verb must go to the end.

questions.stem: Complete: "Er tut so, als ___ er nichts gehört."
questions.explanation: After als on its own, the verb comes straight after it, in the Konjunktiv II for an unreal comparison: "als hätte er nichts gehört". The indicative "hat" is wrong after als alone, "habe gehabt" isn't a form that fits, and "würde" would need an infinitive (würde hören), not a participle.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Sie redet, als ob sie alles allein erfunden hätte.
Sie redet, als ob hätte sie alles allein erfunden.
Sie redet, als hätte erfunden sie alles allein.
Sie redet, als ob sie hätte alles allein erfunden.
questions.explanation: After als ob the verb goes to the end: "als ob sie … erfunden hätte". Only after als alone does the verb come first (als hätte sie … erfunden). The other choices mix the two patterns.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Er tut so, als ob er krank wäre."?
choices: Er tut so, weil er krank ist.
Er ist krank, aber er tut nichts.
Er tut so, als wäre er krank.
Er tut so, obwohl er krank ist.
questions.explanation: als ob + verb at the end and als + verb straight after mean exactly the same. The other sentences state that he really is ill, which the unreal comparison doesn't.

questions.stem: Which sentence expresses a contrast (two different facts side by side) rather than a concession?
choices: Obwohl sie die Beste war, bekam sie die Stelle nicht.
Auch wenn es unbequem ist, müssen wir darüber reden.
In der Stadt gibt es viele Kitas, wohingegen es auf dem Land nur wenige gibt.
Wenngleich das Gesetz es verbietet, kommt Diskriminierung vor.
questions.explanation: wohingegen compares two facts that are simply different: many nurseries in the city, few in the country. The other three are concessions: a fact that should have led to a different result (the best candidate, the law) or a difficulty that doesn't stop the action.

questions.stem: Which sentence fits best in a formal written report?
choices: Obgleich die Lohnlücke kleiner geworden ist, besteht weiterhin Handlungsbedarf.
Obwohl die Lohnlücke halt kleiner ist, muss man doch was tun.
Die Lohnlücke ist kleiner, aber egal, wir müssen was machen.
Klar, die Lohnlücke ist kleiner, trotzdem, ne?
questions.explanation: obgleich and the nominal phrase "es besteht Handlungsbedarf" (there is a need for action) are formal written style. The others use spoken features: the particles halt and doch, "was" for etwas, "egal", "klar" and the tag "ne?".

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Quote ist zwar umstritten, ___ sie hat die Zahl der Frauen in Aufsichtsräten erhöht."
questions.explanation: zwar … aber concedes a point and then makes another: it's controversial, admittedly, but it has worked. sondern only follows a negation, and obwohl or während would send the verb to the end ("hat … erhöht" is in main-clause order here).

questions.stem: Match each connector to its meaning.
questions.explanation: wenngleich = formal although, selbst wenn = even if, wohingegen = whereas (verb at the end), als ob = as if, hingegen = by contrast (adverb, no verb-final order). "unless" is es sei denn or außer wenn from lesson 17.

questions.stem: Complete with one word ("Whatever she says, he contradicts her."): "Was sie ___ sagt, er widerspricht."
questions.explanation: The pattern for "whatever, however, no matter how" is a W-word or so/wie + auch, with the verb at the end: "Was sie auch sagt, …". The main clause then often starts with its own subject: "er widerspricht".

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Es sieht so aus, ___ würde sich die Rollenverteilung langsam ändern."
questions.explanation: The verb (würde) comes straight after the gap, so the word must be als on its own: "als würde sich …". With als ob or als wenn the verb would go to the end: "als ob sich die Rollenverteilung langsam ändern würde".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: He acts as if he hadn't heard anything.
questions.explanation: With als alone, the Konjunktiv II verb comes straight after it: "als hätte er nichts gehört". The version with als ob is also accepted, with the verb at the end: "als ob er nichts gehört hätte". "hat" is the indicative, which doesn't belong in written unreal comparisons.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: Although the law forbids it, discrimination happens.
questions.explanation: The obwohl clause comes first with its verb at the end (verbietet), so the main clause starts with its verb: "kommt Diskriminierung vor" (vorkommen, separable: to happen, occur). "Obwohl es das Gesetz verbietet" (pronoun before the noun subject) is also accepted. "trotzdem" is an adverb and can't introduce a subordinate clause.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio report. What is the main reason the experts give?

audio.text: Laut einer neuen Studie verdienen Frauen in Deutschland im Durchschnitt weiterhin weniger als Männer. Zwar ist die Lücke in den letzten zehn Jahren geschrumpft, sie bleibt jedoch deutlich. Experten führen das vor allem darauf zurück, dass Frauen häufiger in Teilzeit arbeiten.

choices: The gap has grown over the last ten years.
questions.explanation: The report ends: "Experten führen das vor allem darauf zurück, dass Frauen häufiger in Teilzeit arbeiten." The gap has shrunk, not grown ("Zwar ist die Lücke … geschrumpft"), and salary negotiations aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen to the two people disagreeing. What is the second speaker's argument?

audio.text: Ich finde die Quote ungerecht. Es sollte nur die Qualifikation zählen. — Das sehe ich anders. Selbst wenn alle gleich qualifiziert sind, werden Männer häufiger befördert. Ohne Quote ändert sich da nichts.

choices: Even when everyone is equally qualified, men are promoted more often, so a quota is needed.
Quotas are unfair to men and women alike.
questions.explanation: The second speaker says "Selbst wenn alle gleich qualifiziert sind, werden Männer häufiger befördert. Ohne Quote ändert sich da nichts." The first speaker is the one who says only qualifications should count.

questions.stem: Listen. Which statement is true?

audio.text: Sosehr wir uns auch bemüht haben, der Eingang ist immer noch nicht barrierefrei. Allerdings bekommt das Gebäude im Frühjahr einen Aufzug.

choices: Their efforts have made the entrance accessible.
The building got a lift last spring.
They haven't made any effort at all.
The entrance still isn't accessible, but the building is getting a lift in spring.
questions.explanation: "Sosehr wir uns auch bemüht haben" = however hard we tried, the entrance still isn't accessible. "Allerdings bekommt das Gebäude im Frühjahr einen Aufzug" adds a limitation: a lift is coming in spring (bekommt: future meaning).

questions.stem: Which word means the courage to stand up for other people in public?
questions.explanation: die Zivilcourage is moral courage in everyday life, for example intervening when someone is insulted. die Teilhabe is participation in society, die Gleichstellung equality as a policy, and die Emanzipation emancipation.

questions.stem: In an argument, what is "der Einwand"?
questions.explanation: der Einwand (from einwenden, to object) is what the other side says against your position. The claim is die These, the evidence der Beleg, and the conclusion die Schlussfolgerung.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Meines Erachtens ist das zu teuer.
Meines Erachtens das ist zu teuer.
Meiner Erachtens ist das zu teuer.
Meines Erachtens, das ist zu teuer.
questions.explanation: meines Erachtens is a fixed genitive phrase that fills position 1, so the verb follows straight away: "Meines Erachtens ist das …". "Meiner Erachtens" mixes it up with "meiner Meinung nach", and the other two break verb-second.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ kommt, dass die Tierhaltung viele Treibhausgase verursacht."
questions.explanation: "Hinzu kommt, dass …" = in addition, on top of that. "Abgesehen" needs davon or von (abgesehen davon), "Zuletzt kommt" doesn't mean "in addition", and "Hinzufügen" is an infinitive (to add).

questions.stem: Complete in the Präteritum: "Ein Kritiker ___, dass Bio-Fleisch zu teuer sei."
questions.explanation: einwenden is separable and has the irregular Präteritum wandte (wendete is also correct): "Ein Kritiker wandte ein, dass …". In a main clause the prefix goes to the end of the clause, so "einwandte" is wrong here, and the other two aren't real forms.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the most carefully hedged claim?
choices: Vieles spricht dafür, dass Bio-Lebensmittel in der Regel weniger Pestizidrückstände enthalten.
Alle Bio-Lebensmittel sind völlig frei von Pestiziden.
Es ist bewiesen, dass konventionelles Gemüse krank macht.
questions.explanation: "Vieles spricht dafür" and "in der Regel" limit the claim to what evidence supports, and the claim itself is narrow (fewer residues). The others use absolute words (immer, alle, völlig, bewiesen) that are hard to defend.

questions.stem: Which phrase introduces your response to a counterargument?
questions.explanation: "Dem lässt sich entgegenhalten" = against this, one can argue: dem refers back to the counterargument. The others state a position, conclude, or add a last argument.

questions.stem: Put the sentences of this short argument in a logical order.
choices: Ich vertrete die Ansicht, dass Kantinen mehr vegetarische Gerichte anbieten sollten.
Dafür spricht vor allem, dass ein hoher Fleischkonsum dem Klima schadet.
Zwar wenden manche ein, dass die Gäste das nicht wollen.
Dem lässt sich jedoch entgegenhalten, dass vegetarische Gerichte in vielen Mensen schon jetzt sehr beliebt sind.
Alles in allem überwiegen für mich die Vorteile.
questions.explanation: Claim (Ich vertrete die Ansicht), reason (Dafür spricht vor allem), counterargument (Zwar wenden manche ein), response to it (Dem lässt sich jedoch entgegenhalten, where dem points back to the objection), conclusion (Alles in allem).

questions.stem: Which sentence makes a proposal, as the model forum post does?
choices: Kantinen könnten mehr vegetarische Gerichte anbieten.
Kantinen bieten mehr vegetarische Gerichte an.
Kantinen haben mehr vegetarische Gerichte angeboten.
Kantinen sollen mehr vegetarische Gerichte angeboten haben.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv II (könnten) presents an option: canteens could offer more. The present and the Perfekt state facts, and "sollen … angeboten haben" is the hearsay modal from module 1: they are said to have offered.

questions.stem: Which word fits? "Für diese Behauptung gibt es keine ___ Belege."
questions.explanation: stichhaltig = sound, watertight, the adjective for arguments and evidence: there is no sound evidence for this claim. The others are food and farming words that don't describe evidence.

questions.stem: What is "die Massentierhaltung"?
questions.explanation: die Massentierhaltung is intensive livestock farming with many animals in a small space. Animal welfare is das Tierwohl, organic farming der Ökolandbau, and meat consumption der Fleischkonsum.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to what it does in an argument.
questions.explanation: These are the building blocks of a forum post: position, an additional reason, a counterargument, a hedged claim and a conclusion. None of them interrupts anyone; that belongs to spoken discussion (lesson 20).

questions.stem: Complete with one word ("Apart from that, organic meat is also more expensive."): "___ davon ist Bio-Fleisch auch noch teurer."
questions.explanation: "Abgesehen davon" = apart from that. It fills position 1, so the verb follows: "Abgesehen davon ist …". With a noun: abgesehen von + dative (abgesehen vom Preis).

questions.stem: Complete with one word ("Last but not least, the price plays a part."): "Nicht ___ spielt auch der Preis eine Rolle."
questions.explanation: "Nicht zuletzt" = last but not least, not least. Like other phrases in position 1, it is followed directly by the verb (spielt).

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Abgesehen davon das Fleisch ist zu billig.
Nicht zuletzt spielt der Preis eine Rolle.
Alles in allem überwiegen die Vorteile.
Hinzu kommt, dass viele Höfe Subventionen brauchen.
questions.explanation: "Abgesehen davon" fills position 1, so the verb must come next: "Abgesehen davon ist das Fleisch zu billig." The other three sentences have the verb correctly in second place.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: Critics object that organic products are too expensive.
questions.explanation: einwenden is separable: in the main clause the verb is in position 2 and the prefix ein goes to the end of the clause, before the comma: "Kritiker wenden ein, dass …". In the dass clause the verb (sind) goes to the end. The infinitive "einwenden" isn't needed.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: In my view, meat is far too cheap.
questions.explanation: "Meines Erachtens" (genitive, a fixed phrase) can fill position 1, so the verb comes next (Meines Erachtens ist Fleisch viel zu billig), or follow the verb (Fleisch ist meines Erachtens viel zu billig). "Meiner" is the wrong form; the phrase is always meines Erachtens.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio report. Why are more farmers switching to organic farming?

audio.text: Immer mehr Landwirte in der Region stellen auf Ökolandbau um. Der Grund sind nicht nur höhere Preise für Bio-Produkte, sondern auch neue Subventionen des Landes. Allerdings sind die Erträge im ersten Jahr meist geringer.

choices: Because yields are higher in the first year.
Because conventional farming has been banned.
Because people are eating more meat.
Because of higher prices for organic products and new state subsidies.
questions.explanation: The report says: "Der Grund sind nicht nur höhere Preise für Bio-Produkte, sondern auch neue Subventionen des Landes." Yields in the first year are actually lower ("Allerdings sind die Erträge im ersten Jahr meist geringer").

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker think?

audio.text: Ich bin Veganerin, aber ich finde nicht, dass man anderen etwas vorschreiben sollte. Meines Erachtens hilft Information mehr als Verbote.

questions.explanation: The speaker is vegan but says "ich finde nicht, dass man anderen etwas vorschreiben sollte" (people shouldn't be told what to do) and "Meines Erachtens hilft Information mehr als Verbote".

questions.stem: Listen to the lecture extract. According to the speaker, what does a sound argument consist of?

audio.text: Ein stichhaltiges Argument besteht aus einer These, einer Begründung und einem Beleg. Wer nur eine Behauptung aufstellt, ohne sie zu begründen, überzeugt niemanden.

choices: a claim, a reason and evidence
questions.explanation: "Ein stichhaltiges Argument besteht aus einer These, einer Begründung und einem Beleg." The speaker adds that a claim without reasons convinces nobody.

questions.stem: The task asked for four points: your opinion, reasons, what supermarkets could do differently, and your own experience. Read the post: "Ich finde es skandalös, wie viele Lebensmittel bei uns im Müll landen. Supermärkte werfen jeden Abend Brot und Obst weg, obwohl alles noch genießbar ist. Das liegt meines Erachtens daran, dass viele Kunden bis kurz vor Ladenschluss volle Regale erwarten. Hinzu kommt, dass viele Menschen das Mindesthaltbarkeitsdatum falsch verstehen. Ich selbst habe früher oft Joghurt weggeworfen, nur weil das Datum abgelaufen war. Heute probiere ich erst, bevor ich etwas wegwerfe." Which point does the post not cover?
questions.explanation: The opinion is in the first sentence (skandalös), the reasons follow (customers expect full shelves, hinzu kommt …), and the experience is the yoghurt story. But there is no suggestion for supermarkets, for example giving food to a food bank. In the exam, a missing point costs content marks.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich bin nicht gegen Bürgerbeteiligung, ___ gegen schlecht vorbereitete Volksentscheide."
questions.explanation: After a negation, sondern replaces one thing with another: not against participation, but against badly prepared referendums. aber would add a restriction without replacing anything, which doesn't fit here.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Idee ist gut, ___ teuer."
questions.explanation: There is no negation, so sondern is impossible. aber adds a restriction: good, but expensive. denn (because) would need a full clause.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das betrifft nicht nur junge Menschen, ___ Rentner."
questions.explanation: The fixed pair is nicht nur …, sondern auch (not only … but also). "aber auch" is heard in speech but counts as a mistake in standard German, and sondern without auch would mean "not young people, but pensioners" (replacing them).

questions.stem: Which is the most diplomatic way to make a proposal in a discussion?
choices: Wäre es nicht sinnvoller, zuerst die Anwohner zu befragen?
Man muss zuerst die Anwohner befragen.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv II question (Wäre es nicht sinnvoller …?) offers the idea for discussion. The indicative statement, müssen and the imperative all sound like demands that leave the other person no room.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Wenn wir das früher gewusst hätten, hätten wir anders geplant."?
choices: Wir hatten das früher gewusst und anders geplant.
Hätten wir das früher gewusst, hätten wir anders geplant.
Hätten wir das früher gewusst, wir haben anders geplant.
Wir wüssten es früher, wenn wir geplant hätten.
questions.explanation: A conditional clause can drop wenn and start with the verb: "Hätten wir das früher gewusst, …". The main clause stays in the Konjunktiv II. "hatten" is the indicative Plusquamperfekt (a real past), and mixing in "wir haben" breaks both the mood and the word order.

questions.stem: "Nicht ich habe die Petition gestartet." What does this mean?
choices: I haven't started the petition yet.
I started the petition, but not on my own.
It wasn't me who started the petition; someone else did.
questions.explanation: nicht directly before ich negates only that part of the sentence: not me (but someone else, which a sondern phrase could add). To negate the whole action, nicht would go late: "Ich habe die Petition nicht gestartet."

questions.stem: Someone keeps interrupting you. What do you say, politely?
choices: Lassen Sie mich bitte kurz ausreden.
questions.explanation: "Lassen Sie mich bitte ausreden" = please let me finish (speaking). "Seien Sie ruhig!" is rude, the sentence with doch makes no sense, and "Reden Sie bitte aus" asks the other person to finish their sentence, the opposite of what you want.

questions.stem: Which reply concedes a point to the other person?
questions.explanation: "Den Punkt gebe ich Ihnen" = I'll grant you that point. The other three insist or disagree.

questions.stem: Complete: "Da stimme ich ___ zu."
questions.explanation: zustimmen takes the dative: jemandem zustimmen, so "Ich stimme dir zu". dich is the accusative, the most common mistake here; widersprechen also takes the dative (Ich widerspreche dir).

questions.stem: What is "die Wahlbeteiligung"?
choices: the act of casting a vote
questions.explanation: die Wahlbeteiligung is the share of voters who actually vote. The campaign is der Wahlkampf, the right to vote das Wahlrecht, and casting a vote die Stimmabgabe.

questions.stem: Which verb means to give ground, to come round a little?
questions.explanation: einlenken (separable: lenkte ein) = to back down partly, to come round. beharren auf is the opposite (to insist), polarisieren is to divide opinion, and verhandeln is to negotiate.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to what it does in a discussion.
left: Darf ich dazu kurz etwas sagen?
Da haben Sie nicht ganz unrecht.
Wie wäre es mit einem Kompromiss?
Moment, ich war noch nicht fertig.
questions.explanation: These are the main moves in a discussion: asking to speak, holding your position, giving ground, proposing (Konjunktiv II) and defending your turn. Summing up would be, for example, "Dann halten wir fest: …".

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Das ist kein Kompromiss, ___ eine Niederlage."
questions.explanation: kein is a negation, and the second part replaces the first: not a compromise, a defeat. So it must be sondern, not aber.

questions.stem: Make this a polite proposal with the Konjunktiv II of "sein": "___ es nicht besser, die Bürger früher zu beteiligen?"
questions.explanation: "Wäre es nicht besser, …?" = wouldn't it be better …? The Konjunktiv II of sein is wäre (with umlaut); "war" would be the Präteritum, a question about the past.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: Wouldn't it make more sense to ask the residents first?
questions.explanation: A yes/no question starts with the verb (Wäre), then es nicht sinnvoller, then the zu-infinitive clause with zu befragen at the end. "zuerst die Anwohner" and "die Anwohner zuerst" are both fine. "würde" isn't needed: wäre is already the Konjunktiv II.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in German.
questions.prompt: It isn't the politicians who decide, it's the citizens.
questions.explanation: nicht at the very start negates only "die Politiker", and sondern brings in the replacement: "Nicht die Politiker entscheiden, sondern die Bürger." aber doesn't replace anything, so it doesn't fit.

questions.stem: Listen to the discussion. What do the two speakers agree on at the end?

audio.text: Volksentscheide auf Bundesebene wären ein Fortschritt für die Demokratie. — Das sehe ich anders. Sie polarisieren und vereinfachen komplexe Fragen. — Den Punkt gebe ich dir. Aber wie wäre es mit Bürgerräten auf kommunaler Ebene? — Damit könnte ich leben.

questions.explanation: The first speaker concedes ("Den Punkt gebe ich dir") and proposes Bürgerräte auf kommunaler Ebene; the second accepts ("Damit könnte ich leben"). Nationwide referendums were the first speaker's original idea, which the second rejected.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio news. What did the winner announce?

audio.text: Die Wahlbeteiligung bei der Oberbürgermeisterwahl lag gestern bei nur 38 Prozent. Die Wahlsiegerin, Anna Roth, kündigte an, die Bürger künftig stärker an Entscheidungen zu beteiligen.

choices: that the election will be repeated
that she will involve citizens more in decisions in future
that she will lower local taxes
that she will resign because of the low turnout
questions.explanation: The winner "kündigte an, die Bürger künftig stärker an Entscheidungen zu beteiligen". The low turnout (38 percent) is mentioned, but nobody resigns or repeats the election.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's point?

audio.text: Moment, lassen Sie mich bitte ausreden. Ich habe nicht gesagt, dass Petitionen nutzlos sind, sondern dass sie allein nicht reichen.

choices: The other person should stop talking about petitions.
Petitions are enough to change politics.
Petitions on their own aren't enough.
questions.explanation: The speaker corrects a misunderstanding with nicht …, sondern: "Ich habe nicht gesagt, dass Petitionen nutzlos sind, sondern dass sie allein nicht reichen." The tempting wrong answer, "useless", is exactly what the speaker says they did not mean.

questions.stem: Read: "In der Schweiz stimmen die Bürgerinnen und Bürger mehrmals im Jahr über nationale Fragen ab. Wer eine Änderung der Verfassung vorschlagen will, braucht 100.000 gültige Unterschriften. Gegen ein neues Gesetz kann man ein Referendum verlangen, wenn man innerhalb von 100 Tagen 50.000 Unterschriften sammelt. Befürworter sehen darin echte Mitbestimmung. Kritiker hingegen bemängeln die oft niedrige Beteiligung und den großen Einfluss teurer Kampagnen." What do critics object to?
choices: low turnout and the influence of expensive campaigns
that only parliament can call a referendum
questions.explanation: The last sentence, introduced by "Kritiker hingegen" (critics, by contrast), names the low turnout and the influence of expensive campaigns. The text says citizens vote several times a year and need signatures to demand a referendum, so the other answers contradict it.

questions.stem: "Wir wollen eine Stadt, in der Kinder sicher Rad fahren. Wir wollen eine Stadt, in der niemand allein ist. Wir wollen eine Stadt, in der jeder mitreden kann." Which device is this?
questions.explanation: Each sentence begins with the same words (Wir wollen eine Stadt, in der …): that is an anaphora. There is no question, the parts don't clearly rise in intensity, and nothing is meant ironically.

questions.stem: "Wir haben geplant, gestritten und gebaut." Which device is this?
questions.explanation: Three parallel parts (three participles) form a tricolon, which sounds complete to listeners. There is no repeated opening (anaphora) and no question.

questions.stem: Which is the correct way to say "Let's be honest"?
questions.explanation: The first-person plural imperative of sein uses the Konjunktiv I form seien: "Seien wir ehrlich." "Sind wir ehrlich?" is a question (are we honest?), and after "lasst uns" the infinitive is needed (lasst uns ehrlich sein).

questions.stem: You are speaking to a formal audience. Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: To people you address with Sie, the imperative of lassen is "Lassen Sie uns …" + infinitive. "Lasst" is the ihr form, and "Lassen wir uns …" would mean "let's let ourselves …".

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich appelliere ___ Ihre Vernunft."
questions.explanation: appellieren takes an + accusative: an Ihre Vernunft (to your good sense). The noun works the same way: ein Appell an die Jugend.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a rhetorical question?
choices: Wollen wir wirklich, dass unsere Kinder in einer Stadt ohne Bäume aufwachsen?
questions.explanation: A rhetorical question expects no answer because the answer is obvious (no, we don't). The other three are genuine questions asking for information.

questions.stem: Match each device to its example.
choices: Ein Garten ist … Ein Garten ist … Ein Garten ist …
erst Zweifel, dann Ärger, schließlich Wut
Nicht der Staat, sondern die Bürger.
questions.explanation: The anaphora repeats the opening, the rhetorical question needs no answer, the climax rises step by step (doubt, anger, rage), and the contrast uses nicht … sondern. "Lieber spät als nie" is a proverb, not one of these devices.

questions.stem: Which word describes a speech that sweeps the audience along?
questions.explanation: mitreißend (from mitreißen, to carry along) = rousing, stirring. langatmig means long-winded, sachlich matter-of-fact, and bissig biting, sharp.

questions.stem: Listen to the end of the speech. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, seien wir ehrlich: Dieses Jahr war hart. Aber wir haben zusammengehalten, wir haben weitergemacht, und wir haben es geschafft. Lassen Sie uns heute feiern!

questions.explanation: After "seien wir ehrlich: Dieses Jahr war hart" the speaker uses a tricolon (zusammengehalten, weitergemacht, geschafft) and ends with "Lassen Sie uns heute feiern!", let us celebrate today. The hard year is mentioned, but as something they got through.

questions.stem: Listen. Which device does the speaker use?

audio.text: Was bedeutet das für unsere Stadt? Es bedeutet, dass wir jetzt handeln müssen.

choices: a rhetorical question that the speaker answers
questions.explanation: The speaker asks "Was bedeutet das für unsere Stadt?" and answers it straight away: a rhetorical question used to introduce the main point. There is no heckle from the audience, no quotation and no list of three.

questions.stem: What is "ein Zwischenruf" in parliament?
choices: a heckle shouted from the benches
the closing speech of a debate
a written question to the government
questions.explanation: der Zwischenruf (zwischen + rufen) is a shout that interrupts a speaker, a heckle. It is a regular part of debates in the Bundestag.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, why are many modern German speakers careful with heavy "Pathos"?
choices: German has no words for strong feelings.
Pathos is only used in Austria.
It can sound exaggerated or old-fashioned, partly because of how political speeches were used in the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains that zu viel Pathos sounds exaggerated, and that many speakers avoid big emotional gestures partly because of the history of political speeches in the twentieth century. Modern speeches tend to be eindringlich rather than loud. Nothing forbids pathos.

questions.stem: What is a Glosse?
choices: a stage show with satirical sketches
a short, pointed, usually humorous newspaper commentary
questions.explanation: die Glosse is a short humorous commentary, often in a regular column. A cartoon is die Karikatur, and a stage show is das Kabarett.

questions.stem: Which word shows that the writer doesn't accept a label?
questions.explanation: "die sogenannte Reform" = the so-called reform: the writer doubts it deserves the name. nämlich (namely, you see), übrigens (by the way) and tatsächlich (actually, indeed) don't create distance.

questions.stem: In "Die angeblich günstige Lösung hat das Dreifache gekostet", what does "angeblich" signal?
choices: The writer confirms that it was cheap.
The writer doubts the claim that it was cheap.
questions.explanation: angeblich = supposedly, allegedly: it was said to be cheap, but it cost three times as much. The writer reports the claim only to reject it.

questions.stem: Which sentence is most likely meant ironically?
choices: Ein Brötchen kostet in dieser Bäckerei 60 Cent.
Natürlich ist es völlig normal, dass ein Brötchen fünf Euro kostet.
Die Bäckerei öffnet um sechs Uhr.
questions.explanation: natürlich and völlig normal present an absurd price as obvious: a classic irony marker (particles of obviousness where nothing is obvious). The other sentences are plain statements of fact.

questions.stem: Complete: "Sie machen sich ___ seinen Dialekt lustig."
questions.explanation: sich lustig machen über + accusative = to make fun of. The other prepositions don't combine with this phrase.

questions.stem: In the Glosse "Die Smart-Gießkanne", the writer says "Die Inbetriebnahme dauerte nur drei Stunden." What is meant?
choices: Setting it up was pleasantly quick.
The can works for three hours at a time.
The plant needed three hours of water.
Setting it up took far too long; "nur" is ironic.
questions.explanation: Three hours to set up a watering can is absurdly long, so "nur" (only) means the opposite of what it says. Reading it literally misses the irony that the whole Glosse is built on.

questions.stem: At the end of the Glosse, the writer says of Mr Krause, who waters with an old bucket and has the finest tomatoes: "Der Arme." What does this really mean?
choices: The opposite: Mr Krause is the one doing well, without an app.
The writer feels sorry for his tomatoes.
questions.explanation: "Der Arme" (poor man) pretends to pity him for not having an app, but his tomatoes are the best in the street while the writer's geranium died. The pity is ironic, and the real target is the writer's own tech enthusiasm.

questions.stem: What is the real target of the Glosse "Die Smart-Gießkanne"?
choices: our habit of making simple things complicated with technology
questions.explanation: The text mocks the "smart" can that needs an account, a 40-page privacy policy and an update, and contrasts it with a bucket that works. The geranium and Mr Krause are part of the story, not the target.

questions.stem: Match each term to its description.
choices: a stage show with satirical monologues and sketches
a drawing that exaggerates to make a point
someone who writes a regular column
questions.explanation: Kabarett is the stage form, the Glosse the newspaper form, the Karikatur the drawn form, and the Kolumnist writes a regular column (often a Glosse). A news agency report is meant to be neutral, the opposite of satire.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract from a Kabarett show. What is being mocked?

audio.text: Unsere Regierung hat ein neues Programm gegen die Bürokratie beschlossen. Es umfasst nur 600 Seiten und tritt in Kraft, sobald drei weitere Formulare ausgefüllt sind.

choices: bureaucracy, even in a programme against bureaucracy
questions.explanation: A programme against bureaucracy that has "nur 600 Seiten" and comes into force only once three more forms are filled in: the exaggeration and the ironic "nur" mock bureaucracy itself.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker really mean?

audio.text: Ein toller Service! Ich habe nur vier Stunden in der Warteschleife verbracht.

choices: The service was bad; the praise is ironic.
Four hours is a short time to wait.
They enjoyed the music while on hold.
questions.explanation: "Ein toller Service!" followed by "nur vier Stunden in der Warteschleife" is ironic praise: nur marks an absurdly long time as short. Without the irony markers, you might take the praise literally.

questions.stem: Which word means a passing dig at someone?
questions.explanation: der Seitenhieb (literally a blow from the side) is a brief critical remark in passing: ein Seitenhieb auf die Regierung. der Spott is mockery in general, die Übertreibung exaggeration, die Pointe a punchline.
